findings: Circular/inconsistent precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md section 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2
The SOW starts before the MSA effective date, even though it is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md section 2.2

The SOW programme is 36 months, but the MSA initial term is only 24 months, so the programme extends beyond the initial contractual term and depends on renewal not being terminated. 01_msa.md sections 3.1-3.3; 02_sow.md section 2.1
Conflicting monthly Fee amounts: £12,400 in the MSA and £12,800 in the SOW. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1
Conflicting payment periods: 30 days after receipt in the MSA and 45 days after receipt in the SOW. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3

Conflicting acceptance mechanics: the MSA requires express written acceptance, while the SOW provides deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3
The MSA refers to acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md entire document

Deliverables are not actually listed in the SOW; they are said to be in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, leaving the contractual Deliverables undefined and potentially unilaterally changeable. 02_sow.md section 6.1; 01_msa.md section 1.3
No acceptance criteria are provided in Schedule 1 despite the MSA requiring Deliverables to be assessed against them. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md section 6
Conflicting liability caps: the MSA cap is the Fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months, while the SOW cap is £250,000. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2

The MSA says its liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum, but the DPA says no limitation or exclusion in the Agreement applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
The SOW excludes indirect and consequential loss, but the DPA says no exclusion of liability applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 02_sow.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
Conflicting professional indemnity insurance requirements: £5,000,000 in the MSA and £2,000,000 in the SOW. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Conflicting audit rights: the MSA limits Customer to receiving Provider's SOC 2 report and says Customer has no further audit/inspection rights, while the DPA grants an annual audit including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md section 9

Internal inconsistency in the MSA records provisions: Provider must make records available on reasonable request, but only 'in accordance with clause 10.2', which states Customer has no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems. 01_msa.md sections 10.2 and 12.2

Conflicting data retention/deletion duties: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry or termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry or termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2

The DPA deletion trigger is only expiry or termination of the Agreement; if the SOW terminates but the MSA continues, there is no clear deletion obligation for Customer Personal Data processed for the terminated SOW. 02_sow.md sections 2.3-2.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2

Conflicting confidentiality definitions: the MSA treats information as Confidential Information only if marked confidential at disclosure, while the DPA says all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4

Conflicting subcontracting/subprocessing consent standards: the MSA allows subcontracting without Customer consent, while the DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Potentially incompatible processing locations: the SOW delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while the DPA permits processing Customer Personal Data only in the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved processing locations. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2
Conflicting availability service levels: the SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md section 7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

Conflicting start point for service levels: the SOW applies platform service levels only from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA states availability obligations without that limitation. 02_sow.md section 7.1; 04_sla.md section 3

Conflicting service credit caps and mechanics: the SOW allows service credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps them at 10% and requires automatic application to the next invoice. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md sections 4.1-4.2

The service credit amount is not calculable: the SOW says credits are 'up to' 25% and the SLA states only an entitlement and cap, but neither provides a formula or scale for calculating the credit. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4

The SLA says service credits are Customer's sole financial remedy for failure to meet availability, which conflicts with broader remedies and liability positions elsewhere, especially the DPA's no-limitation rule if an availability failure involves data protection breach. 04_sla.md section 4.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1; 01_msa.md section 13

Conflicting definitions of Business Day: the MSA uses Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, while the SLA uses Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1

SLA response and resolution times are measured from Provider's acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response-time obligation circular because acknowledgement is itself the response event. 04_sla.md section 5.4

Conflicting definitions of Security Incident: the DPA definition is broad and includes unauthorised or unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; the SLA definition is narrower and requires confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of Customer data. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Conflicting Security Incident notification obligations: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
The SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

Conflicting governing law provisions: the MSA is governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA says the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md section 15.1; 03_dpa.md section 13.2

The MSA gives exclusive jurisdiction to the courts of England and Wales for disputes under the Agreement, but the DPA separately selects Irish governing law without addressing jurisdiction, creating an incomplete and conflicting dispute framework. 01_msa.md section 15.2; 03_dpa.md section 13

Conflicting service report retention periods: the SLA requires service reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement, while the MSA requires records, data and materials relating to the Agreement to be retained for 7 years after expiry or termination. 04_sla.md section 6.3; 01_msa.md section 12.4

The SLA treats a Security Incident as a Priority 1 Incident requiring Resolution within 4 hours, but a data security incident involving loss or corruption of data may not be capable of being resolved by restoration of service or a workaround within that target. 04_sla.md sections 1.6, 5.1 and 7.2

The SLA excludes responsibility for unavailability caused by a third-party service outside Provider's control, but the MSA and DPA make Provider responsible for subcontractors/subprocessors. The clauses conflict if the third party is Provider's subcontractor or subprocessor. 04_sla.md section 9.2; 01_msa.md section 9.1; 03_dpa.md section 5.3
The SOW refers to 'named key personnel' and restricts substitution, but no named key personnel are identified. 02_sow.md section 3.5
Support hours are stated as 08:00 to 18:00, but no time zone is specified. 04_sla.md section 2.2
The SOW requires the delivery lead to be available during Customer's working hours, but 'Customer's working hours' is not defined. 02_sow.md section 3.3

The DPA says Annex 1 sets out the processing details in full, but Annex 1 does not clearly state the nature of the processing despite section 3.1 identifying nature as part of the processing description. 03_dpa.md sections 3.1, 3.4 and Annex 1
The MSA uses the term 'Addendum' in the definition of Agreement but does not define what qualifies as an Addendum. 01_msa.md section 1.1
The MSA renewal clause says the Agreement renews unless terminated under clause 3.3, but does not refer to immediate termination for material breach under clause 3.4. 01_msa.md sections 3.2-3.4

The SLA requires automatic application of service credits to the next invoice, but gives no mechanism for payment or refund if there is no next invoice, such as in the final service month. 04_sla.md section 4.1

findings: Circular/inconsistent order of precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while the SOW says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md clause 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2
The SOW programme starts before the MSA is effective, even though the SOW is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date and clause 3.1; 02_sow.md section 2.2

The SOW requires a 36-month programme, but the MSA initial term is only 24 months and there is no express provision that the SOW survives MSA expiry or termination. 01_msa.md clause 3.1; 02_sow.md section 2.1
Conflicting monthly Fee amounts: the MSA states £12,400, while the SOW states £12,800. 01_msa.md clause 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1
Conflicting payment periods: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, while the SOW allows 45 days. 01_msa.md clause 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3

Conflicting acceptance mechanism: the MSA requires express written acceptance and says no Deliverable is accepted until then, while the SOW provides for deemed acceptance after five Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md clause 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3
Broken cross-reference: the MSA requires assessment against acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md clause 6.2; 02_sow.md generally

Deliverables are not actually identified in the SOW; the SOW says they are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, conflicting with the MSA definition requiring Deliverables to be identified in a Statement of Work. 01_msa.md clause 1.3; 02_sow.md section 6.1

Acceptance criteria for Deliverables are missing from the SOW, despite the MSA requiring Customer to assess Deliverables against Schedule 1 acceptance criteria. 01_msa.md clause 6.2; 02_sow.md section 6
Conflicting liability caps: the MSA cap is Fees paid or payable in the preceding 12 months, while the SOW cap is £250,000. 01_msa.md clauses 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2

Conflicting liability treatment for data protection breaches: the DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law, while the MSA says its liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum. 01_msa.md clauses 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
Conflicting professional indemnity insurance requirements: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md clause 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4
Conflicting availability commitments: the SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md section 7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

Conflicting start date for availability obligations: the SOW applies service levels only from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA states an availability obligation without that delayed start. 02_sow.md section 7.1; 04_sla.md section 3
Conflicting service credit caps: the SOW allows service credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps them at 10%. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2
Service credit amount is not determinable: the SOW says credits are “up to” 25% but gives no formula or bands for calculating the actual credit. 02_sow.md section 7.4

Service credit amount is not determinable: the SLA creates an entitlement to a service credit and gives only a 10% cap, but gives no formula or bands for calculating the actual credit. 04_sla.md section 4

Potentially conflicting remedies for availability failures: the SLA says service credits are the sole financial remedy for failure to meet availability, while the MSA contains general remedies/liability provisions and the SOW creates service-credit rights without saying they are exclusive. 01_msa.md section 13; 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.3

Conflicting definition of Business Day: the MSA defines it as Monday to Friday excluding public holidays in England and Wales, while the SLA defines it as Monday to Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md clause 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1

Conflicting subcontracting/subprocessor consent rules: the MSA allows Provider to subcontract without Customer consent, while the DPA requires Customer’s prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md clause 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Conflicting audit rights: the MSA says Customer has no audit/inspection/attendance rights beyond receiving the annual SOC 2 Type II report, while the DPA gives Customer an annual audit right including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md clause 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

Internal inconsistency in MSA records access: clause 12.2 says Provider must make records available on reasonable request in accordance with clause 10.2, but clause 10.2 says Customer has no audit, inspection or premises/systems access right beyond the SOC 2 report. 01_msa.md clauses 10.2 and 12.2

Conflicting confidentiality scope: the MSA protects only information marked confidential at disclosure, while the DPA states all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md clause 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4

Conflicting retention/deletion obligations for Customer Personal Data: the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry or termination, while the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for seven years after expiry or termination. 01_msa.md clause 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2

Conflicting retention periods for service reports: the SLA requires retention only for the duration of the Agreement, while the MSA requires records relating to the Agreement to be retained for seven years after expiry or termination. 01_msa.md clause 12.4; 04_sla.md section 6.3

Conflicting processing locations: the SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while the DPA permits processing of Customer Personal Data only in the UK and EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

Conflicting international transfer position: the SOW contemplates service delivery from India, but the DPA prohibits transfers of Customer Personal Data outside the UK/EEA without prior written authorisation and an appropriate transfer mechanism; no such authorisation or mechanism is included. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md section 4.2

Conflicting definitions of Security Incident: the DPA definition is broad and covers unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; the SLA definition is narrower and requires confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Conflicting Security Incident notice timing: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirmation. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
Broken cross-reference: the SLA says Security Incident escalation contacts are listed in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

Conflicting governing law: the MSA says the Agreement and disputes are governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA says the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md clause 15.1; 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

The DPA creates a governing-law conflict but no matching jurisdiction clause for DPA disputes, while the MSA gives exclusive jurisdiction to the courts of England and Wales. 01_msa.md clause 15.2; 03_dpa.md section 13
The SOW refers to “named key personnel” but does not identify any named key personnel. 02_sow.md section 3.5

Incident response and resolution times are measured only from Provider’s acknowledgement in its service management tool, allowing Provider to delay acknowledgement and preventing measurement from the actual report/detection of the Incident. 04_sla.md section 5.4

Security Incident notice under the SLA is to Customer’s nominated security contact, but the nominated security contact is not identified in the contract set and the referenced escalation annex does not exist. 04_sla.md sections 7.3-7.4

findings: Circular/inconsistent precedence: the MSA says it prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while the SOW says the SOW prevails over the MSA for conflicts. 01_msa.md clause 14.2; 02_sow.md clause 1.2

The MSA defines “Agreement” as including Schedules and Addenda, but the precedence clause then contrasts “this Agreement” with Schedules/Addenda, making the hierarchy internally ambiguous. 01_msa.md clauses 1.1 and 14.2
SOW programme commences before the MSA effective date, even though the SOW is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md clause 2.2
SOW programme duration is 36 months, but the MSA initial term is only 24 months, creating a mismatch unless renewal occurs. 01_msa.md clause 3.1; 02_sow.md clause 2.1
Termination-for-convenience notice periods conflict: 90 days under the MSA versus 30 days for the SOW. 01_msa.md clause 3.3; 02_sow.md clause 2.3
Monthly Fee conflicts: £12,400 under the MSA versus £12,800 under the SOW. 01_msa.md clause 4.1; 02_sow.md clause 5.1
Payment period conflicts: invoices payable within 30 days under the MSA versus 45 days under the SOW. 01_msa.md clause 4.3; 02_sow.md clause 5.3
Acceptance rules conflict: the MSA requires express written acceptance, while the SOW provides for deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md clause 6.1; 02_sow.md clause 6.3
MSA requires acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW has no Section 12. 01_msa.md clause 6.2; 02_sow.md generally

Deliverables are said to be listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, not in the SOW itself, conflicting with the MSA definition of Deliverable as an item identified in a Statement of Work and leaving deliverables/criteria uncertain. 01_msa.md clause 1.3; 02_sow.md clause 6.1

Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked, but the MSA defines Confidential Information only as information marked confidential at disclosure. 01_msa.md clause 11.1; 03_dpa.md clause 1.4

MSA permits subcontracting without Customer consent, but the DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor where Customer Personal Data is processed. 01_msa.md clause 9.3; 03_dpa.md clause 5.1

MSA states Customer has no audit/inspection rights beyond receiving the annual SOC 2 Type II report, but the DPA grants annual audit rights including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md clause 10.2; 03_dpa.md clauses 9.1-9.2

MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry/termination, but the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md clause 12.4; 03_dpa.md clause 8.2

Liability caps conflict: MSA cap is the fees paid/payable in the preceding 12 months and says it applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum, while the SOW sets a £250,000 cap. 01_msa.md clauses 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md clause 9.2

DPA excludes all Agreement limitations/exclusions for DPA/Data Protection Law breaches, conflicting with the MSA liability cap and the MSA statement that its cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum. 01_msa.md clauses 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md clause 11.1
Professional indemnity insurance limits conflict: £5,000,000 under the MSA versus £2,000,000 under the SOW. 01_msa.md clause 16.1; 02_sow.md clause 9.4

Governing law conflicts: the MSA applies England and Wales law to the Agreement and disputes, while the DPA applies Republic of Ireland law to the DPA and disputes arising out of it. 01_msa.md clause 15.1; 03_dpa.md clause 13.2

Processing/location obligations conflict with delivery location: DPA permits processing only in the UK/EEA and approved locations are London and Dublin, but the SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India. 02_sow.md clause 3.4; 03_dpa.md clauses 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

Business Day is defined differently: Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays in the MSA, but Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays in the SLA. 01_msa.md clause 1.2; 04_sla.md clause 1.1
Availability service level conflicts: 99.5% under the SOW versus 99.9% under the SLA. 02_sow.md clause 7.2; 04_sla.md clause 3.1

Timing of availability obligations conflicts: SOW applies service levels from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA states availability obligations without that delayed start. 02_sow.md clause 7.1; 04_sla.md section 3
Service credit caps conflict: SOW allows credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps credits at 10%. 02_sow.md clause 7.4; 04_sla.md clause 4.2

Service credit mechanics are incomplete: both SOW and SLA state entitlement/caps but do not provide a calculation or scale for the amount of credit due after an availability failure. 02_sow.md clause 7.4; 04_sla.md clauses 4.1-4.2

SLA says service credits are Customer’s sole financial remedy for availability failures, which conflicts with the SOW’s separate service credit regime and potentially narrows remedies for breach of the SOW service levels. 02_sow.md clause 7.4; 04_sla.md clause 4.3

Security Incident is defined differently: the DPA definition is broad and covers unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; the SLA definition is narrower and requires confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of Customer data. 03_dpa.md clause 1.6; 04_sla.md clause 7.1

Security Incident notice periods conflict: DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness, while SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md clause 6.1; 04_sla.md clause 7.3

Security Incident recipient requirements are inconsistent/incomplete: DPA requires notice to Customer, while SLA requires notice to Customer’s nominated security contact, but that contact is not identified. 03_dpa.md clause 6.1; 04_sla.md clause 7.3
SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md clause 7.4; 03_dpa.md generally

SLA service report retention conflicts with MSA record retention: SLA requires retention only for the duration of the Agreement, while MSA requires records relating to the Agreement to be retained for 7 years after expiry/termination. 04_sla.md clause 6.3; 01_msa.md clause 12.4

Response and Resolution targets are measured from Provider’s acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response-time target circular or ineffective because Provider controls when the measurement starts. 04_sla.md clause 5.4
SOW restricts substitution of named key personnel, but no named key personnel are actually identified. 02_sow.md clause 3.5

MSA allows disclosure of Confidential Information only to personnel who need to know, but also permits subcontracting without consent; subcontractors are not expressly included as permitted recipients, creating an internal inconsistency for subcontracted services requiring confidential information. 01_msa.md clauses 9.3 and 11.2
DPA section titled “Precedence” does not state any operative precedence rule, leaving DPA conflicts with the MSA/Schedules unresolved except by the MSA’s conflicting hierarchy. 03_dpa.md section 12

findings: Circular/inconsistent precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md section 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2
SOW 1 commences before the MSA effective date, even though it is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md section 2.2

The MSA initial term is 24 months, but SOW 1 requires a 36-month programme, creating a mismatch in service duration unless renewal occurs and is not terminated. 01_msa.md sections 3.1-3.3; 02_sow.md section 2.1

Termination for convenience notice periods conflict: the MSA requires at least 90 days' notice, while SOW 1 allows termination of the SOW on 30 days' notice. 01_msa.md section 3.3; 02_sow.md section 2.3
Monthly Fee conflicts: the MSA states £12,400 per month, while SOW 1 states £12,800 per month. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1
Payment period conflicts: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt of an undisputed invoice, while SOW 1 allows 45 days. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3

Acceptance provisions conflict: the MSA requires express written acceptance and says no Deliverable is accepted otherwise, while SOW 1 provides for deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3
The MSA refers to acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but SOW 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md

SOW 1 does not actually list Deliverables or acceptance criteria; it refers to a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, leaving the contractual Deliverables and criteria outside the executed SOW. 02_sow.md sections 6.1-6.4
SOW 1 says named key personnel cannot be substituted without Customer approval, but no named key personnel are identified. 02_sow.md sections 3.2 and 3.5
Availability service level conflicts: SOW 1 requires 99.5% monthly availability from Phase 3, while the SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability. 02_sow.md sections 7.1-7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1
Service credit cap conflicts: SOW 1 allows service credits of up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps service credits at 10% of the monthly Fee. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2

Service credit mechanics conflict: the SLA says credits are applied automatically and are the sole financial remedy, while SOW 1 only states an entitlement of up to 25% and does not make them the sole remedy. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md sections 4.1 and 4.3

Liability cap conflicts: the MSA caps aggregate liability at Fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 caps Provider liability at £250,000. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2

The DPA conflicts with the MSA liability regime by stating that no limitation or exclusion of liability in the Agreement applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

The SOW exclusion of indirect or consequential loss conflicts with the DPA statement that no exclusion of liability applies to DPA or Data Protection Law breaches. 02_sow.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
Professional indemnity insurance requirement conflicts: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while SOW 1 requires at least £2,000,000. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Business Day is defined inconsistently: the MSA uses Monday to Friday excluding public holidays in England and Wales, while the SLA uses Monday to Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1

The SLA response-time targets are circular or ineffective because response and resolution times are measured from the point Provider acknowledges the Incident, even though response time is itself supposed to measure how quickly Provider responds. 04_sla.md sections 5.1-5.4

Security Incident is defined inconsistently: the DPA covers any unauthorised or unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA only covers confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Security Incident notification timing conflicts: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirmation. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
The SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

Processing location obligations conflict with the SOW delivery location: the DPA permits processing only in the UK/EEA and lists London and Dublin, while SOW 1 says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India. 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2; 02_sow.md section 3.4

The DPA is internally inconsistent on transfers: it says Customer Personal Data may be processed only within the UK/EEA, but also contemplates transfers outside those territories with Customer authorisation and an appropriate transfer mechanism. 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.2

Subcontracting/subprocessing consent conflicts: the MSA permits Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA requires prior written consent for each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Audit rights conflict: the MSA limits Customer to receiving Provider's annual SOC 2 Type II report and denies any further audit, inspection or premises/system access, while the DPA grants annual audits including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

The MSA is internally inconsistent on records access: it requires Provider to make records available on reasonable request, but only in accordance with clause 10.2, which denies further audit or inspection rights beyond the SOC 2 report. 01_msa.md sections 10.2 and 12.2

Retention/deletion obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry or termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry or termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md sections 8.2-8.3

Confidential Information is defined inconsistently: the MSA covers only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure, while the DPA states all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4

Governing law conflicts: the MSA applies the laws of England and Wales to the Agreement, while the DPA states that the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md section 15.1; 03_dpa.md section 13.2

The DPA is internally inconsistent on governing law: clause 13.1 says the DPA is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement, but clause 13.2 says the DPA is governed by the laws of the Republic of Ireland. 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

The SLA availability calculation is ambiguous: it gives a formula using total minutes in the month, then says agreed maintenance windows are excluded, but does not specify how excluded maintenance affects the numerator and denominator. 04_sla.md sections 3.2-3.3

The SLA availability calculation is ambiguous: it gives a formula using total minutes in the month, then says agreed maintenance windows are excluded, but does not specify how excluded maintenance affects the numerator and denominator. 04_sla.md sections 3.2-3.3

findings: Circular/contradictory precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while the SOW says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md section 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2
SOW programme starts before the MSA effective date, even though the SOW is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md section 2.2

SOW requires a 36-month programme, but the MSA initial term is only 24 months and the documents do not clearly state what happens to the SOW if the MSA expires or is terminated before programme completion. 01_msa.md section 3.1; 02_sow.md sections 2.1-2.2

Termination notice periods conflict: the MSA requires at least 90 days' notice for convenience termination, while the SOW allows termination of the SOW on 30 days' notice. 01_msa.md section 3.3; 02_sow.md section 2.3
Monthly Fee conflicts: the MSA states £12,400, while the SOW states £12,800. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1
Payment period conflicts: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, while the SOW allows 45 days. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3

Acceptance mechanism conflicts: the MSA requires express written acceptance and says no Deliverable is accepted until then, while the SOW provides for deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3
The MSA refers to acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md

Deliverables are not actually listed in the SOW; they are said to be in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, leaving contractual Deliverables unidentified and potentially unilaterally changeable. 02_sow.md section 6.1
The SOW does not state acceptance criteria for Deliverables, despite the MSA requiring assessment against Schedule 1 acceptance criteria. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md section 6

IP assignment trigger is unclear because Provider assigns IP in Deliverables only on payment in full 'for them', but the contract sets monthly service Fees rather than deliverable-specific prices. 01_msa.md sections 4.1 and 7.2; 02_sow.md section 5

Subcontracting consent conflicts: the MSA allows Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Confidentiality restrictions appear incompatible with subcontracting/subprocessing: the MSA permits disclosure only to personnel who need to know, while the DPA contemplates disclosure of Customer Personal Data to approved Subprocessors. 01_msa.md section 11.2; 03_dpa.md section 5

Audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no further right to audit, inspect, or attend Provider premises or systems beyond receiving the SOC 2 report, while the DPA grants audit rights including inspection of premises, systems, and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

Records access provisions are internally inconsistent: the MSA requires Provider to make records available on reasonable request but only 'in accordance with clause 10.2', which says Customer has no further audit/inspection rights. 01_msa.md sections 10.2 and 12.2

Retention/deletion obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data, and materials relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry/termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2

Service report retention conflicts: the SLA requires retaining monthly service reports only for the duration of the Agreement, while the MSA requires records relating to the Agreement to be retained for 7 years after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 04_sla.md section 6.3

Confidential Information definition conflicts: the MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure, while the DPA says all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4

Confidentiality survival is inconsistent with personal-data confidentiality: MSA confidentiality obligations expire after 3 years, while the DPA treats all Customer Personal Data as Confidential Information without a matching 3-year limit and also requires deletion after termination. 01_msa.md section 11.3; 03_dpa.md sections 1.4 and 8.2

Liability cap conflicts: the MSA caps aggregate liability at the prior 12 months' Fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum, while the SOW caps Provider liability at £250,000. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2

DPA liability provision conflicts with the MSA: the DPA says no Agreement limitation or exclusion applies to DPA/Data Protection Law breaches, but the MSA says its liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

DPA indemnity for fines conflicts with the MSA liability regime because the DPA creates uncapped indemnity exposure while the MSA purports to impose a cap notwithstanding any Addendum. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.2
Insurance requirement conflicts: the MSA requires professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Processing location conflicts: the DPA permits Customer Personal Data processing only in the UK/EEA and lists London and Dublin, while the SOW says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

The DPA's definition of Data Protection Law depends on territories where Services are provided; the SOW provides Services from India, but the DPA otherwise restricts processing to the UK/EEA, creating uncertainty over applicable data protection law and permitted processing locations. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 1.2 and 4.1

Approved processing locations are inconsistent with the DPA's stated full processing details if the replatforming Services are performed from Bengaluru, because Annex 1 says processing is for the replatforming and hosting Services but Annex 2 lists only London and Dublin. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md Annexes 1 and 2

Governing law conflicts: the MSA is governed by England and Wales law with exclusive England and Wales jurisdiction, while the DPA says disputes under the DPA are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md sections 15.1-15.2; 03_dpa.md section 13.2

DPA governing law clause is internally inconsistent: clause 13.1 says the DPA is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement except as provided in 13.2, but 13.2 then states the DPA and any dispute arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2
DPA processing category wording is inconsistent: section 3.3 refers to 'loyalty scheme identifiers', while Annex 1 refers to 'loyalty identifiers'. 03_dpa.md section 3.3 and Annex 1

Business Day is defined differently: the MSA uses Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, while the SLA uses Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1
Availability service level conflicts: the SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md section 7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

Availability obligations start at different times: the SOW applies service levels from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA states an availability obligation without limiting it to Phase 3 or any platform go-live date. 02_sow.md section 7.1; 04_sla.md section 3.1
Service credit caps conflict: the SOW allows service credits of up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps service credits at 10%. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2

Service credit remedy conflicts: the SLA says service credits are Customer's sole financial remedy for failure to meet availability, while the SOW grants credits without saying they are exclusive and the MSA has general remedies/liability provisions. 01_msa.md section 13; 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.3

Security Incident definition conflicts: the DPA defines it broadly to include unauthorised or unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss, or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA limits it to confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of Customer data. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Security Incident notification timing conflicts: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2; Annex 3 does not exist. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md
The SLA requires notice to Customer's nominated security contact, but no nominated security contact is identified in the contract set. 04_sla.md section 7.3
The SOW restricts substitution of named key personnel, but no named key personnel are actually named. 02_sow.md section 3.5
Customer's working hours are referenced but not defined, creating uncertainty over the delivery lead's required availability. 02_sow.md section 3.3

Response and Resolution times in the SLA are measured from when Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool; this makes the 'response' target circular or ineffective because the clock starts only after Provider has acknowledged the Incident. 04_sla.md sections 5.1-5.4
Maintenance-window notice period depends on the SLA's conflicting Business Day definition, so the required 5 Business Days' notice is uncertain. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md sections 1.1 and 3.4

findings: Circular/inconsistent precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule/Addendum, while SOW 1 says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md section 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2
SOW 1 commences before the MSA effective date, even though it is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md section 2.2
The SOW requires a 36-month programme, but the MSA initial term is only 24 months, leaving the programme extending beyond the initial contractual term. 01_msa.md section 3.1; 02_sow.md section 2.1
Termination-for-convenience notice periods conflict: 90 days under the MSA versus 30 days for the SOW. 01_msa.md section 3.3; 02_sow.md section 2.3
Monthly Fee conflicts: £12,400 under the MSA versus £12,800 under SOW 1. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1
Payment period conflicts: invoices are payable within 30 days under the MSA but within 45 days under SOW 1. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3

Acceptance mechanism conflicts: the MSA requires express written acceptance, while SOW 1 provides for deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3
The MSA requires assessment against acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but SOW 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md entire document

Deliverables are said to be listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, not in the SOW itself, conflicting with the MSA definition of Deliverable as an item identified in a Statement of Work and leaving deliverables outside the executed contract text. 01_msa.md section 1.3; 02_sow.md section 6.1
No acceptance criteria are actually set out for the deliverables, despite the MSA requiring acceptance criteria in Schedule 1. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md section 6

Liability cap conflicts: the MSA uses a rolling 12-month fees cap and says it applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum, while SOW 1 sets a £250,000 cap. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2

Data protection liability conflicts: the DPA says no Agreement limitation or exclusion applies to DPA/Data Protection Law breaches, while the MSA caps liability and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

The SOW excludes indirect or consequential loss, but the DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law, creating a conflict for data-protection-related indirect or consequential losses. 02_sow.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
Professional indemnity insurance limits conflict: £5,000,000 under the MSA versus £2,000,000 under SOW 1. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Audit rights conflict: the MSA limits Customer to receiving Provider's annual SOC 2 Type II report and gives no further audit/inspection rights, while the DPA permits annual audits including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

Internal MSA tension: Provider must make records available on reasonable request, but only in accordance with clause 10.2, which says Customer has no further audit, inspection or attendance rights beyond the SOC 2 report. 01_msa.md sections 10.2 and 12.2

Definition of Confidential Information conflicts: the MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure, while the DPA makes all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4

Confidentiality disclosure rights are too narrow for the subcontracting/subprocessing structure: the MSA permits disclosure only to personnel who need to know, while other documents contemplate subcontractors/subprocessors who may need access. 01_msa.md sections 9 and 11.2; 03_dpa.md section 5

Retention/deletion conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry/termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2

Processing-location conflict: the DPA restricts Customer Personal Data processing to the UK/EEA and lists London and Dublin as approved locations, while SOW 1 states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

Subcontracting/subprocessing consent conflict: the MSA allows Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA requires Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Governing law conflicts: the MSA says the Agreement and disputes are governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA says the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md section 15.1; 03_dpa.md section 13.2

Internal DPA governing-law inconsistency: clause 13.1 says the DPA is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement except as provided in 13.2, but 13.2 then states that the DPA itself is governed by Irish law, making 13.1 effectively contradicted for the whole DPA. 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

Business Day is defined inconsistently: Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays in the MSA, but Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays in the SLA. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1
Availability service level conflicts: SOW 1 requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md section 7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1
Service credit caps conflict: SOW 1 allows service credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps them at 10%. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2

Service credit process conflicts: SOW 1 gives Customer an entitlement to service credits, while the SLA requires Provider to apply them automatically without a claim. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.1

No service-credit calculation methodology is provided; the documents state only maximum percentages, so the actual credit due for a given availability failure is undefined. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4

Service-level commencement conflicts or is unclear: SOW 1 says platform service levels apply from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA states availability obligations without any Phase 3 limitation or start date. 02_sow.md section 7.1; 04_sla.md section 3.1

Security Incident is defined inconsistently: the DPA definition is broad and includes unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA definition is limited to confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of Customer data. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Security Incident notification deadlines conflict: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware, while the SLA allows 72 hours from confirmation. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
The SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2; Annex 3 does not exist. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

SLA response-time measurement is circular/defective: response times are measured from Provider's acknowledgement of the Incident, so the deadline for response starts only after the response/acknowledgement has already occurred. 04_sla.md sections 5.1-5.4
Support hours use 08:00 to 18:00 but no time zone is specified. 04_sla.md section 2.2

Service report retention conflicts: the SLA requires retaining service reports only for the duration of the Agreement, while the MSA requires Provider to retain records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 04_sla.md section 6.3
SOW 1 restricts substitution of named key personnel, but no named key personnel are identified. 02_sow.md section 3.5
The delivery lead must be available during Customer's working hours, but Customer's working hours are not defined. 02_sow.md section 3.3

The DPA says Annex 1 sets out the processing details in full, but Annex 1 omits or only minimally states key details such as the nature of processing and any specific processing operations. 03_dpa.md section 3.4 and Annex 1

The DPA's processing-location provisions are ambiguous: clause 4.1 appears to permit processing anywhere in the UK/EEA, while clause 4.3 and Annex 2 list only London and Dublin as approved processing locations. 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

DPA internal inconsistency: clause 13.1 says the DPA is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement except as provided in clause 13.2, while clause 13.2 then states the entire DPA is governed by Irish law, effectively contradicting the general statement. 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2
DPA section titled 'Precedence' does not actually state any order of precedence or conflict rule. 03_dpa.md section 12

Business Day definition conflict: the MSA defines Business Day as Monday to Friday excluding public holidays in England and Wales, while the SLA defines Business Day as Monday to Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1
Availability service level conflict: SOW 1 requires 99.5% monthly availability from Phase 3, while the SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability. 02_sow.md sections 7.1-7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

Service credit cap conflict: SOW 1 allows service credits of up to 25% of the monthly Fee for availability failure, while the SLA caps monthly service credits at 10% of the monthly Fee. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2

Service credit process conflict: the SLA says service credits are applied automatically without a Customer claim, while SOW 1 only says Customer is entitled to service credits and does not provide the same automatic mechanism. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.1

Sole remedy conflict: the SLA says service credits are Customer's sole financial remedy for failure to meet availability, which conflicts with the broader liability and remedy framework in the MSA and with SOW 1's separate availability-credit provision. 01_msa.md section 13; 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.3

Security Incident definition conflict: the DPA defines Security Incident broadly to include unauthorised or unlawful access to, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA defines it narrowly as confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Security Incident notification deadline conflict: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3

Security Incident notification recipient mismatch: the DPA requires notice to Customer, while the SLA requires notice to Customer's nominated security contact; the contract set does not identify that security contact. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
Non-existent reference: the SLA says Security Incident escalation contacts are listed in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md Annexes

Response-time measurement is defective: SLA response and resolution times are measured from Provider's acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response target circular or ineffective because the clock starts only when Provider has already acknowledged/responded. 04_sla.md section 5.4
Key personnel clause is incomplete: SOW 1 restricts substitution of named key personnel, but no named key personnel are identified in the contract set. 02_sow.md section 3.5

Approved processing locations are incomplete for the stated service model: the DPA lists London and Dublin only, while the SOW requires a delivery team in Bengaluru; the documents do not state whether Bengaluru personnel may access systems or Customer Personal Data. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md Annex 2

Phase deliverables are controlled unilaterally by the delivery lead rather than fixed in the executed SOW, creating uncertainty and conflicting with the MSA requirement that Deliverables be identified in a Statement of Work. 01_msa.md section 1.3; 02_sow.md section 6.1
unmatched: SOW 1 commences before the MSA effective date, even though it is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md section 2.2

Deliverables are not actually identified in the SOW: the MSA defines Deliverables as items identified in a Statement of Work, but SOW 1 says they are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, which is not part of the contract set. 01_msa.md section 1.3; 02_sow.md section 6.1

DPA internal inconsistency: clause 13.1 says the DPA is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement except as provided in clause 13.2, while clause 13.2 then states the entire DPA is governed by Irish law, effectively contradicting the general statement. 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

findings: The order of precedence is directly inconsistent: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while the SOW says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md section 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2
The DPA section headed “Precedence” does not actually state any precedence rule, leaving conflicts involving the DPA unresolved except by the MSA default rule. 03_dpa.md section 12
The SOW is issued under the MSA but states that the programme commences on 1 March 2027, one month before the MSA Effective Date of 1 April 2027. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md section 2.2

The SOW requires a 36-month programme, but the MSA has only a 24-month initial term and may be terminated for convenience on 90 days’ notice, making the status of the remaining programme period uncertain. 01_msa.md sections 3.1-3.3; 02_sow.md section 2.1
The monthly Fee is inconsistent: the MSA states £12,400, while the SOW states £12,800 for the same Services. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1
Payment timing is inconsistent: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, while the SOW allows 45 days. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3

Termination notice for convenience is inconsistent: the MSA requires at least 90 days’ notice to terminate the Agreement, while the SOW allows termination of the SOW on 30 days’ notice. 01_msa.md section 3.3; 02_sow.md sections 2.3-2.4

Acceptance is inconsistent: the MSA says no Deliverable is accepted unless expressly accepted in writing, while the SOW provides for deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days without response. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3
The MSA requires Deliverables to be assessed against acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md

Deliverables are not actually listed in the SOW; instead they are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, which conflicts with the MSA definition requiring Deliverables to be identified in a Statement of Work. 01_msa.md section 1.3; 02_sow.md section 6.1

Because Deliverables are in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, the scope may be changed outside the written change-control process required by the MSA. 01_msa.md section 2.4; 02_sow.md section 6.1
The SOW refers to “named key personnel” but does not identify any named key personnel, making the substitution restriction incomplete or inoperative. 02_sow.md section 3.5
“Customer’s working hours” is not defined, so the delivery lead availability obligation lacks a clear time zone or schedule. 02_sow.md section 3.3
Professional indemnity insurance limits are inconsistent: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires at least £2,000,000. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Liability caps are inconsistent: the MSA caps each party’s liability at Fees paid or payable in the preceding 12 months, while the SOW caps Provider’s liability at £250,000. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2

The SOW liability cap does not repeat the MSA carve-outs for death, personal injury caused by negligence, and fraud, creating an inconsistency over whether those liabilities are capped. 01_msa.md section 13.2; 02_sow.md section 9.2

The DPA says no limitation or exclusion of liability in the Agreement applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law, but the MSA says its liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
The DPA indemnity for fines is inconsistent with the MSA liability cap and the MSA rule that the cap applies notwithstanding any Addendum. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.2

The SOW exclusion of indirect or consequential loss conflicts with the DPA rule that no limitation or exclusion applies to DPA or Data Protection Law breaches. 02_sow.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

Audit rights are inconsistent: the MSA says Customer has no right beyond receiving the annual SOC 2 Type II report, while the DPA allows annual audits including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md section 9

The MSA is internally inconsistent on records access: it says records must be made available on reasonable request, but only in accordance with a clause that denies further audit, inspection or attendance rights. 01_msa.md sections 10.2 and 12.2

Retention/deletion obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry or termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry or termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md sections 8.2-8.3

Confidential Information is defined inconsistently: the MSA covers only information marked confidential in writing, while the DPA says all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4

Subcontracting/subprocessing consent is inconsistent: the MSA permits subcontracting without Customer consent, while the DPA prohibits engaging any Subprocessor without Customer’s prior written consent to that specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Processing location obligations conflict with the SOW delivery location: the DPA permits processing only in the UK/EEA and lists London and Dublin, while the SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

The DPA definition of Data Protection Law depends on territories where the Services are provided, but the DPA simultaneously restricts processing to the UK/EEA while the SOW provides for Services from India, creating uncertainty over applicable law and permitted processing locations. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 1.2 and 4.1

Governing law is inconsistent: the MSA says the Agreement and disputes are governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA says the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md sections 15.1-15.2; 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

“Business Day” is defined inconsistently: the MSA uses Monday to Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, while the SLA uses Monday to Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1
Availability service levels conflict: the SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md section 7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

The date from which availability service levels apply is inconsistent: the SOW applies them from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA states the availability obligation without that delayed start. 02_sow.md section 7.1; 04_sla.md section 3
Service credit caps conflict: the SOW allows credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps credits at 10% of the monthly Fee. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2
The service credit provisions do not provide a calculation formula or tiers, so the actual credit for a given availability failure is uncertain. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md sections 4.1-4.2

The SLA says service credits are Customer’s sole financial remedy for availability failure, which is inconsistent with broader remedies and liability provisions elsewhere in the contract set and may conflict with uncapped DPA remedies if an outage involves data protection breaches. 01_msa.md section 13; 03_dpa.md section 11; 04_sla.md section 4.3

“Security Incident” is defined inconsistently: the DPA uses a broad definition covering unauthorised or unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of Customer data. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Security Incident notification timing conflicts: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware, while the SLA allows 72 hours after confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3

Security Incident notification recipients are inconsistent or incomplete: the DPA requires notice to Customer, while the SLA requires notice to Customer’s nominated security contact, which is not identified in the contract set. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
The SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2; Annex 3 does not exist. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

SLA response and resolution times are measured from the point Provider acknowledges the Incident, making the response-time target circular and allowing Provider to delay the start of the clock by delaying acknowledgement. 04_sla.md section 5.4
unmatched: Deliverables are not actually listed in the SOW; instead they are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, which conflicts with the MSA definition requiring Deliverables to be identified in a Statement of Work. 01_msa.md section 1.3; 02_sow.md section 6.1

Because Deliverables are in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, the scope may be changed outside the written change-control process required by the MSA. 01_msa.md section 2.4; 02_sow.md section 6.1
The SOW refers to “named key personnel” but does not identify any named key personnel, making the substitution restriction incomplete or inoperative. 02_sow.md section 3.5
“Customer’s working hours” is not defined, so the delivery lead availability obligation lacks a clear time zone or schedule. 02_sow.md section 3.3

The SOW liability cap does not repeat the MSA carve-outs for death, personal injury caused by negligence, and fraud, creating an inconsistency over whether those liabilities are capped. 01_msa.md section 13.2; 02_sow.md section 9.2

The date from which availability service levels apply is inconsistent: the SOW applies them from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA states the availability obligation without that delayed start. 02_sow.md section 7.1; 04_sla.md section 3
The service credit provisions do not provide a calculation formula or tiers, so the actual credit for a given availability failure is uncertain. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md sections 4.1-4.2

SLA response and resolution times are measured from the point Provider acknowledges the Incident, making the response-time target circular and allowing Provider to delay the start of the clock by delaying acknowledgement. 04_sla.md section 5.4

findings: Circular precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 says the SOW prevails over the MSA for conflicts. 01_msa.md section 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2
The SOW programme starts before the MSA effective date, even though the SOW is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md section 2.2

The MSA initial term is 24 months, but the SOW requires a 36-month programme; the programme extends beyond the committed initial MSA term unless renewal occurs. 01_msa.md section 3.1; 02_sow.md section 2.1

The MSA says it continues for an initial 24-month term but also allows either party to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice without limiting that right to after the initial term, undermining the fixed initial term. 01_msa.md sections 3.1 and 3.3
Different monthly Fees are stated for the same Services: £12,400 in the MSA and £12,800 in the SOW. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1
Payment period conflicts: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt of an undisputed invoice, while the SOW allows 45 days. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3
Acceptance mechanism conflicts: the MSA requires express written acceptance, while the SOW deems acceptance after five Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3

The MSA requires Deliverables to be assessed against acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW has no Section 12 and no clear acceptance criteria. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md generally

Deliverables are not actually listed in the SOW; instead they are in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, which conflicts with the MSA definition requiring Deliverables to be identified in a Statement of Work. 01_msa.md section 1.3; 02_sow.md section 6.1

The SOW allows Deliverables to be controlled by a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, potentially permitting changes outside the written bilateral change-control process required by the MSA. 01_msa.md section 2.4; 02_sow.md section 6.1
The SOW refers to 'named key personnel' but does not name any key personnel, making the substitution restriction uncertain. 02_sow.md section 3.5

Business Day is defined differently: the MSA uses Monday to Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, while the SLA uses Monday to Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1
Availability service level conflicts: the SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md section 7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

The start date for availability obligations conflicts or is unclear: the SOW applies service levels only from Phase 3, while the SLA states availability obligations without that limitation. 02_sow.md section 7.1; 04_sla.md section 3
Service credit caps conflict: the SOW allows credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps credits at 10%. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2

Service credit process conflicts: the SLA requires Provider to apply credits automatically without a claim, while the SOW only states Customer is entitled to credits and does not provide the same automatic mechanism. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.1

Service credit provisions are internally incomplete because neither the SOW nor the SLA provides a formula or scale for calculating the actual credit amount, only a maximum cap. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4

The SLA says service credits are Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failure, which conflicts with the broader contractual remedies and liability regime in the MSA and with uncapped liability under the DPA where an availability failure is also a data protection breach. 01_msa.md section 13; 03_dpa.md section 11.1; 04_sla.md section 4.3

Liability caps conflict: the MSA caps liability by reference to Fees paid/payable in the preceding 12 months and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum, while the SOW states a £250,000 cap. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2

The DPA makes breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law uncapped, directly conflicting with the MSA cap and the MSA clause stating the cap applies notwithstanding any Addendum. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

The DPA indemnity for fines arising from data protection breaches conflicts with the MSA liability cap if the MSA cap applies to all claims under the Agreement. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.2
Insurance requirements state different minimum limits: £5,000,000 in the MSA and £2,000,000 in the SOW. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Processing location obligations conflict with the delivery model: the SOW says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while the DPA permits processing only in the UK and EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1 and Annex 2

The DPA prohibits transfers of Customer Personal Data outside the UK/EEA without prior written authorisation and a transfer mechanism, but the SOW mandates an India-based delivery centre without providing that authorisation or mechanism. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md section 4.2

Subcontracting/subprocessing consent conflicts: the MSA permits subcontracting without Customer consent, while the DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no audit, inspection, or premises/systems access beyond receiving the SOC 2 report, while the DPA gives Customer annual audit rights including inspection of premises, systems, and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1 and 9.2

Record/data retention conflicts with deletion: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data, and materials relating to the Agreement for seven years after expiry or termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry or termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2

Confidential Information is defined inconsistently: the MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure, while the DPA says all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4

The MSA confidentiality clause permits disclosure only to personnel who need to know, but other provisions permit subcontractors/Subprocessors; the contract does not reconcile whether Confidential Information may be disclosed to those third parties. 01_msa.md sections 9 and 11.2; 03_dpa.md section 5

Security Incident is defined differently: the DPA covers any unauthorised or unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss, or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Security Incident notification timing conflicts: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3

Security Incident notification recipient is inconsistent: the DPA requires notice to Customer, while the SLA requires notice to Customer's nominated security contact; no single required recipient is reconciled. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
The SLA references escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2; Annex 3 does not exist. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

SLA response and resolution targets are measured from Provider's acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response-time obligation circular because the response clock starts only once Provider has acknowledged/responded. 04_sla.md section 5.4

Governing law conflicts: the MSA is governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA states that the Addendum and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md section 15.1; 03_dpa.md section 13.2

Jurisdiction and governing law are not aligned for DPA disputes: the MSA gives exclusive jurisdiction to England and Wales courts for disputes arising out of the Agreement, while the DPA applies Irish law to DPA disputes without addressing jurisdiction. 01_msa.md section 15.2; 03_dpa.md section 13.2
