findings: Circular/incompatible precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while the SOW says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md section 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2
The SOW programme starts before the MSA effective date, even though it is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md section 2.2

The SOW requires a 36-month programme, while the MSA has only a 24-month initial term; the SOW cannot be completed within the initial term unless renewal occurs. 01_msa.md section 3.1; 02_sow.md section 2.1
Conflicting monthly Fee amounts: the MSA states £12,400, while the SOW states £12,800 for the Services. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1
Conflicting payment periods: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt of an undisputed invoice, while the SOW allows 45 days. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3

Conflicting termination notice periods for the same services structure: the MSA requires 90 days' notice to terminate for convenience, while the SOW allows termination of the SOW on 30 days' notice, leaving unclear what fees/services remain under the MSA. 01_msa.md section 3.3; 02_sow.md sections 2.3-2.4

Conflicting acceptance mechanics: the MSA requires express written acceptance, while the SOW provides for deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3
The MSA requires assessment against acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md

Deliverables are not actually identified in the SOW, despite the MSA defining Deliverables as items identified in a SOW; the SOW instead refers to a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead. 01_msa.md section 1.3; 02_sow.md section 6.1
Acceptance criteria are missing from the SOW, despite the MSA requiring Deliverables to be assessed against Schedule 1 acceptance criteria. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md section 6
The SOW restricts substitution of named key personnel, but no key personnel are named. 02_sow.md section 3.5

Conflicting liability caps: the MSA caps liability at 12 months' Fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum, while the SOW caps Provider liability at £250,000. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2

Conflicting data-protection liability position: the MSA applies its liability cap notwithstanding any Addendum, while the DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
The SOW excludes indirect or consequential loss, while the DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 02_sow.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
Conflicting professional indemnity insurance requirements: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires at least £2,000,000. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Conflicting audit rights: the MSA limits Customer to receiving an annual SOC 2 Type II report and denies further audit/inspection rights, while the DPA gives Customer audit rights including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

Internal inconsistency in the MSA: Provider must make records available on request in accordance with clause 10.2, but clause 10.2 says Customer has no further audit, inspection or premises/systems access rights and does not establish a records-access process. 01_msa.md sections 10.2 and 12.2

Conflicting data retention/deletion obligations: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry/termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md sections 8.2-8.3

Conflicting confidentiality scope: the MSA protects only information marked confidential at disclosure, while the DPA states all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4

Subcontracting/subprocessing conflict: the MSA allows subcontracting any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

The MSA permits subcontracting but the confidentiality clause allows disclosure only to personnel who need to know, not to subcontractors, creating an internal conflict if subcontractors need Confidential Information. 01_msa.md sections 9.3 and 11.2

Processing location conflict: the SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while the DPA permits Customer Personal Data processing only in the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

Conflicting governing law: the MSA is governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA states that the DPA and disputes arising from it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md section 15.1; 03_dpa.md section 13.2

Internal inconsistency in the DPA governing-law clause: clause 13.1 says the DPA is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement except as provided in clause 13.2, but clause 13.2 then governs the entire DPA by Irish law, leaving clause 13.1 effectively displaced. 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

Conflicting definitions of Business Day: the MSA uses Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, while the SLA uses Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1
Conflicting availability commitments: the SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability from Phase 3, while the SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability. 02_sow.md sections 7.1-7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

Conflicting service credit caps/remedies for availability failures: the SOW allows credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps credits at 10% and makes them the sole financial remedy. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md sections 4.2-4.3
The SOW states service credits are 'up to' 25% of the monthly Fee but provides no formula or trigger scale for calculating the actual credit. 02_sow.md section 7.4

The SLA requires service credits to be applied automatically to the next invoice, but the MSA prohibits set-off, deduction or withholding except as required by law or agreed by Provider in writing; the interaction is unclear. 01_msa.md section 4.5; 04_sla.md section 4.1
The basis for calculating service credits is unclear because 'monthly Fee' is defined differently in the MSA and SOW. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1; 04_sla.md sections 4.2 and 7.4

Conflicting Security Incident definitions: the DPA definition covers any unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA definition is narrower and requires confirmed unauthorised access causing loss or corruption of Customer data. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Conflicting Security Incident notification deadlines: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness, while the SLA allows 72 hours after confirmation. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
The SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

SLA response-time targets are circular/ineffective because response and resolution times are measured from the point Provider acknowledges the Incident; the response target is therefore measured from Provider's own acknowledgement rather than from report or occurrence. 04_sla.md sections 5.1-5.4

The SLA requires monthly service reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement, while the MSA requires all records relating to the Agreement to be retained for 7 years after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 04_sla.md section 6.3

Acceptance provisions conflict: the MSA requires express written acceptance and says no Deliverable is accepted until then, while the SOW provides deemed acceptance after five Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3
The MSA refers to acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md generally

Deliverables are not actually identified in the SOW as required by the MSA definition; the SOW instead refers to a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, which is not included in the contract set. 01_msa.md sections 1.3 and 6.2; 02_sow.md section 6.1
The SOW restricts substitution of 'named key personnel', but no key personnel are named. 02_sow.md section 3.5

Processing/location conflict: the SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while the DPA permits processing Customer Personal Data only in the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

Subcontracting consent provisions conflict for subprocessors: the MSA permits subcontracting without Customer consent, while the DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no audit/inspection/access rights beyond receiving the SOC 2 report, while the DPA grants annual audit rights including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

Confidential Information is defined inconsistently: the MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure, while the DPA makes all Customer Personal Data Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4

Retention/deletion obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for seven years after expiry/termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2

Internal retention/confidentiality gap: the MSA requires retention of records, data and materials for seven years after expiry/termination, but confidentiality obligations expire after three years, leaving retained confidential materials unprotected for the remaining period. 01_msa.md sections 11.3 and 12.4

Liability caps conflict: the MSA caps each party's aggregate liability at the prior 12 months' Fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum, while the SOW caps Provider's liability at £250,000. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2

DPA liability conflicts with the MSA liability regime: the DPA says no limitation or exclusion in the Agreement applies to DPA or Data Protection Law breaches, while the MSA says its cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
The SOW excludes indirect and consequential loss, but the DPA says no exclusion of liability applies to breach of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 02_sow.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
Professional indemnity insurance minimums conflict: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires at least £2,000,000. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Governing law conflicts: the MSA is governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA says the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md section 15.1; 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

Business Day is defined inconsistently: the MSA uses Monday to Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, while the SLA uses Monday to Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1
Availability service levels conflict: the SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability from Phase 3, while the SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability. 02_sow.md sections 7.1-7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

Service credit remedies conflict: the SOW allows service credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps them at 10%, requires automatic application, and makes them the sole financial remedy for availability failure. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md sections 4.1-4.3

Security Incident is defined inconsistently: the DPA covers any unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA only covers confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Security Incident notification timing conflicts: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
The SLA references escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

Response and Resolution measurement is internally defective: response times are measured from when Provider acknowledges the Incident, making the response target circular or meaningless because acknowledgement is itself the response trigger. 04_sla.md sections 5.1-5.4
Support hours specify 08:00 to 18:00 but do not state the applicable time zone. 04_sla.md section 2.2

Service report retention conflicts: the SLA requires retaining service reports only for the duration of the Agreement, while the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for seven years after expiry/termination. 04_sla.md section 6.3; 01_msa.md section 12.4

findings: Conflicting order of precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md §14.2; 02_sow.md §1.2
SOW 1 commences on 1 March 2027, one month before the MSA effective date of 1 April 2027, even though it is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md §2.2
The MSA initial term is 24 months, but SOW 1 requires a 36-month programme. The programme extends beyond the MSA initial term unless renewal occurs. 01_msa.md §3.1; 02_sow.md §§2.1, 4.1-4.4
Conflicting convenience termination notice periods: the MSA requires at least 90 days' notice, while SOW 1 permits termination of the SOW on 30 days' notice. 01_msa.md §3.3; 02_sow.md §2.3
Conflicting monthly Fee amounts: the MSA states £12,400, while SOW 1 states £12,800 for the same Services. 01_msa.md §4.1; 02_sow.md §5.1
Conflicting payment periods: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, while SOW 1 requires payment within 45 days of receipt. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3
The MSA requires express written acceptance of Deliverables, but SOW 1 provides for deemed acceptance after five Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md §6.1; 02_sow.md §6.3
The MSA refers to acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but SOW 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md §6.2; 02_sow.md

SOW 1 says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, not in the SOW itself, which conflicts with the MSA definition requiring Deliverables to be identified in a Statement of Work. 01_msa.md §1.3; 02_sow.md §6.1
The contract contains no actual acceptance criteria for Deliverables despite requiring assessment against acceptance criteria. 01_msa.md §6.2; 02_sow.md §6
Conflicting liability caps: the MSA caps liability at Fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months, while SOW 1 caps Provider liability at £250,000. 01_msa.md §13.1; 02_sow.md §9.2

The MSA says its liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum, but the DPA says no limitation or exclusion in the Agreement applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 01_msa.md §13.3; 03_dpa.md §11.1
The DPA indemnity for fines is not reconciled with the MSA liability cap, and the MSA purports to override Addendum liability provisions. 01_msa.md §§13.1, 13.3; 03_dpa.md §11.2
Conflicting professional indemnity insurance requirements: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while SOW 1 requires at least £2,000,000. 01_msa.md §16.1; 02_sow.md §9.4

Conflicting audit rights: the MSA limits Customer to receiving Provider's SOC 2 Type II report and grants no further audit or inspection rights, while the DPA allows annual audits including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md §10.2; 03_dpa.md §§9.1-9.2

Internal tension in the MSA: Provider must make records available to Customer on reasonable request, but only in accordance with clause 10.2, which says Customer has no further audit, inspection or premises/systems access rights. 01_msa.md §§10.2, 12.2

Conflicting retention/deletion duties: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for seven years after expiry or termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry or termination. 01_msa.md §12.4; 03_dpa.md §§8.2-8.3

Conflicting confidentiality definition: the MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure, while the DPA states all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md §11.1; 03_dpa.md §1.4

Conflicting subcontracting/subprocessing consent rights: the MSA permits Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA requires Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §5.1

SOW 1 states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, but the DPA permits processing of Customer Personal Data only in the UK and EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved processing locations. 02_sow.md §3.4; 03_dpa.md §§4.1, 4.3 and Annex 2

Conflicting governing law provisions: the MSA is governed by the laws of England and Wales, while the DPA states that the DPA and disputes arising from it are governed by the laws of the Republic of Ireland. 01_msa.md §15.1; 03_dpa.md §13.2
Internal inconsistency in the DPA governing law clause: §13.1 says the DPA is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement, but §13.2 says the DPA is governed by Irish law. 03_dpa.md §§13.1-13.2

Conflicting definitions of Business Day: the MSA uses Monday to Friday excluding public holidays in England and Wales, while the SLA uses Monday to Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md §1.2; 04_sla.md §1.1
The SLA's support hours state 08:00 to 18:00 on Business Days but do not specify a time zone. 04_sla.md §2.2
Conflicting availability commitments: SOW 1 requires 99.5% monthly availability from Phase 3, while the SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability. 02_sow.md §§7.1-7.2; 04_sla.md §3.1
Conflicting service credit caps: SOW 1 allows service credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps monthly service credits at 10% of the monthly Fee. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §4.2

The service credit mechanism is incomplete: SOW 1 says credits are 'up to' 25% and the SLA caps credits at 10%, but neither document states how the actual credit amount is calculated. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §4

The SLA says service credits are Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, which conflicts with SOW 1's separate credit entitlement and may conflict with the MSA/DPA liability regime where an availability failure also involves other breaches. 04_sla.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §7.4; 01_msa.md §13; 03_dpa.md §11

Conflicting Security Incident definitions: the DPA covers any unauthorised or unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption. 03_dpa.md §1.6; 04_sla.md §7.1

Conflicting Security Incident notification deadlines: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md §6.1; 04_sla.md §7.3
The SLA refers to escalation contacts listed in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md §7.4; 03_dpa.md
SOW 1 prohibits substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement, but no named key personnel are identified. 02_sow.md §3.5

findings: Circular/inconsistent precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md section 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2

No tie-breaker is provided for conflicts between schedules/addenda of the same level, despite multiple conflicts between SOW 1, the DPA and the SLA. 01_msa.md section 14; 02_sow.md; 03_dpa.md; 04_sla.md
The SOW programme begins before the MSA effective date, even though the SOW is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md section 2.2

The SOW requires a 36-month programme, while the MSA has only a 24-month initial term and does not expressly state that SOW 1 survives or extends the MSA term. 01_msa.md section 3.1; 02_sow.md section 2.1
Different monthly Fee amounts are stated for the same Services: £12,400 in the MSA and £12,800 in SOW 1. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1
Payment periods conflict: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, while SOW 1 allows 45 days. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3

Acceptance provisions conflict: the MSA says no Deliverable is accepted unless expressly accepted in writing, while SOW 1 provides deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3
The MSA refers to acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but SOW 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md

SOW 1 does not actually list the Deliverables in the SOW; it refers to a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, creating uncertainty and conflicting with the MSA definition of Deliverable as an item identified in a Statement of Work. 01_msa.md section 1.3; 02_sow.md section 6.1

The phase plan is maintained by the delivery lead, but changes to Services must be agreed in writing by both parties; unilateral maintenance of the deliverables plan may conflict with the MSA change-control requirement. 01_msa.md section 2.4; 02_sow.md section 6.1
SOW 1 restricts substitution of named key personnel, but no named key personnel are identified. 02_sow.md section 3.5
“Customer's working hours” is used but not defined. 02_sow.md section 3.3

Liability caps conflict: the MSA cap is based on Fees paid/payable in the preceding 12 months and applies notwithstanding schedules/addenda, while SOW 1 caps liability at £250,000. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2

The DPA says no Agreement limitation or exclusion applies to DPA or Data Protection Law breaches, but the MSA says its liability limit applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum. 01_msa.md section 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
Insurance requirements conflict: the MSA requires professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000, while SOW 1 requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Subcontracting/subprocessor consent conflicts: the MSA permits subcontracting without Customer consent, while the DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

The MSA confidentiality clause permits disclosure only to personnel who need to know and does not expressly permit disclosure to subcontractors/subprocessors, despite other provisions allowing subcontracting/subprocessing. 01_msa.md sections 9 and 11.2; 03_dpa.md section 5

Processing/location obligations conflict: SOW 1 says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while the DPA permits processing only in the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved processing locations. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

The DPA requires prior written authorisation and a transfer mechanism for transfers outside the UK/EEA, but no such authorisation or mechanism is provided for the Bengaluru delivery location. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md section 4.2

Confidential Information is defined inconsistently: the MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing, while the DPA states all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4

Audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no audit/inspection/right to attend Provider premises or systems beyond receiving the annual SOC 2 report, while the DPA grants annual audits including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

MSA records-access wording is internally inconsistent: Provider must make records available on reasonable request, but only in accordance with clause 10.2, which denies further audit/inspection rights. 01_msa.md sections 10.2 and 12.2

Retention/deletion obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry/termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2

Service-report retention conflicts with the MSA record-retention period: the SLA requires service reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement, while the MSA requires records relating to the Agreement to be retained for 7 years after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 04_sla.md section 6.3

Governing law conflicts: the MSA is governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA says the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md section 15.1; 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

The DPA governing-law clause is internally awkward: clause 13.1 applies the Agreement law except as provided in 13.2, but 13.2 then applies Irish law to the entire DPA and all disputes arising out of it. 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

The DPA changes governing law but does not include a corresponding jurisdiction clause, while the MSA gives exclusive jurisdiction to the courts of England and Wales. 01_msa.md section 15.2; 03_dpa.md section 13

Business Day is defined inconsistently: the MSA uses Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, while the SLA uses Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1
Availability service levels conflict: SOW 1 requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md section 7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

The start date for service levels conflicts or is unclear: SOW 1 applies platform service levels from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA states availability obligations without limiting them to Phase 3. 02_sow.md section 7.1; 04_sla.md section 3
Service credit caps conflict: SOW 1 allows service credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps monthly service credits at 10%. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2

Service credit mechanics conflict: the SLA requires automatic application to the next invoice, while SOW 1 only states that Customer is entitled to credits and does not provide automatic application. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.1

Service credit amounts are indeterminate: SOW 1 says credits are “up to” 25% and the SLA caps credits at 10%, but neither provides a calculation table or formula for the actual credit amount. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4

The SLA states service credits are Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, which may conflict with broader remedies and liability provisions in the MSA/SOW for breach of service obligations. 01_msa.md sections 8 and 13; 02_sow.md section 7; 04_sla.md section 4.3

Security Incident is defined inconsistently: the DPA definition is broad and covers unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA definition is limited to confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Security Incident notification deadlines conflict: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness, while the SLA allows 72 hours after confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
The SLA references escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

The SLA requires notice to Customer's nominated security contact, but the contract set does not identify that contact or provide a mechanism specific to security contacts beyond the general single point of contact. 04_sla.md section 7.3; 01_msa.md section 5.2

Response and Resolution times are measured from when Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own service management tool, which lets Provider control the start time and makes the response-time obligation circular or ineffective. 04_sla.md section 5.4

Maintenance windows are excluded only if agreed, but the SLA separately says Provider need only give 5 Business Days' notice and does not state whether Customer agreement is required. 04_sla.md sections 3.3-3.4 and 9.3

IP assignment timing is unclear because Provider assigns IP in Deliverables on payment in full “for them,” but the contract uses a monthly service Fee and does not allocate payment to individual Deliverables. 01_msa.md sections 4 and 7.2

Conflicting data-protection liability treatment: the MSA liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum, but the DPA says no limitation or exclusion in the Agreement applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 01_msa.md clauses 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

Conflict between SOW exclusion of indirect/consequential loss and DPA statement that no exclusion of liability applies to DPA or Data Protection Law breaches. 02_sow.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

Conflicting governing law: the MSA says the Agreement and disputes are governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA says the Addendum and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law, even though the DPA forms part of the Agreement. 01_msa.md section 15; 03_dpa.md sections 12.1 and 13.2
Conflicting professional indemnity insurance requirements: £5,000,000 in the MSA and £2,000,000 in SOW 1. 01_msa.md clause 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Conflicting Business Day definitions: the MSA defines Business Day as Monday to Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, while the SLA defines it as Monday to Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md clause 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1

SOW 1 says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, but the DPA allows Customer Personal Data to be processed only in the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

The DPA requires prior written authorisation and an appropriate transfer mechanism for transfers outside the UK/EEA, but SOW 1 places the delivery team in India without including such authorisation or mechanism. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md section 4.2
SOW 1 restricts substitution of named key personnel, but no named key personnel are identified in the SOW. 02_sow.md section 3.5
Conflicting platform availability levels: SOW 1 requires 99.5% monthly availability from Phase 3, while the SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability. 02_sow.md sections 7.1-7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

Conflicting service credit caps for availability failure: SOW 1 allows credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps credits at 10% of the monthly Fee. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2

The SLA makes service credits the sole financial remedy for availability failures, but SOW 1 contains a separate service credit regime and the MSA/DPA liability provisions do not align with that exclusive-remedy wording. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.3; 01_msa.md section 13; 03_dpa.md section 11

Conflicting Security Incident definitions: the DPA broadly covers unauthorised or unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Conflicting Security Incident notification deadlines/triggers: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
The SLA refers to Security Incident escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

SLA response-time measurement is defective: response and Resolution times run from when Provider acknowledges the Incident, so the response clock starts only after the response/acknowledgement has already occurred and Provider can delay acknowledgement without breaching the measured target. 04_sla.md section 5.4

The MSA confidentiality obligation survives for only 3 years after expiry or termination, but the MSA also requires Provider to retain records, data and materials for 7 years, leaving retained confidential materials potentially unprotected for the remaining 4 years. 01_msa.md clauses 11.3 and 12.4

findings: Circular/inconsistent precedence: the MSA says it prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while the SOW says the SOW prevails over the MSA for conflicts. 01_msa.md section 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2

The DPA section titled “Precedence” does not actually state any order of precedence, leaving conflicts with the MSA and other schedules unresolved except by the MSA’s general precedence clause. 03_dpa.md section 12
The SOW programme starts before the MSA effective date, even though it is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md sections 1.1 and 2.2

The MSA initial term is 24 months, but the SOW requires a 36-month programme and does not clearly state that the SOW survives or extends the MSA if the MSA is not renewed or is terminated. 01_msa.md section 3.1; 02_sow.md section 2.1

Conflicting convenience termination notice periods: the MSA requires at least 90 days’ notice, while the SOW allows termination of the SOW on 30 days’ notice. 01_msa.md section 3.3; 02_sow.md section 2.3
Conflicting monthly Fee amounts: the MSA states £12,400, while the SOW states £12,800 for the same Services. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1
Conflicting payment periods: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, while the SOW allows 45 days. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3

The MSA prohibits set-off, deduction or withholding except as required by law or agreed by Provider, while the SLA requires automatic service credits to be applied to the next invoice, creating tension over invoice deductions/credits. 01_msa.md section 4.5; 04_sla.md section 4.1

Conflicting acceptance regimes: the MSA requires express written acceptance, while the SOW provides for deemed acceptance after five Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3
The MSA requires Deliverables to be assessed against acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW has no Section 12 and no stated acceptance criteria. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md

The SOW says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, but that phase plan is not included, annexed, or described as an executed contract document, leaving the contractual Deliverables uncertain. 02_sow.md section 6.1
The SOW refers to “named key personnel,” but no named key personnel are identified in the SOW. 02_sow.md section 3.5

Conflicting audit rights: the MSA says Customer has no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider’s premises or systems beyond receiving the SOC 2 report, while the DPA gives Customer a right to audit premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

Conflicting confidentiality definitions: the MSA protects only information marked confidential at disclosure, while the DPA states all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4

Conflicting retention/deletion obligations: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for seven years after expiry or termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry or termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2

Conflicting record retention period for service reports: the MSA requires retention of records for seven years after expiry or termination, while the SLA requires service reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 04_sla.md section 6.3

Conflicting liability caps: the MSA caps liability at Fees paid or payable in the preceding 12 months, while the SOW caps Provider’s liability at £250,000. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2

Conflicting liability treatment for DPA breaches: the MSA says its liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum, while the DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 01_msa.md section 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
Conflicting insurance requirements: the MSA requires professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Conflicting governing law: the MSA says the Agreement and disputes are governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA says the Addendum and disputes arising out of it are governed by the laws of the Republic of Ireland. 01_msa.md section 15.1; 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

Conflicting definitions of “Business Day”: the MSA uses Monday to Friday excluding public holidays in England and Wales, while the SLA uses Monday to Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1

Conflicting subcontracting/subprocessing consent rights: the MSA allows Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA requires Customer’s prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Conflicting processing locations: the SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while the DPA permits processing Customer Personal Data only in the UK and EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2
Conflicting availability commitments: the SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability. 02_sow.md section 7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

Conflicting start of availability obligations: the SOW applies platform service levels from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA states availability obligations without limiting them to Phase 3 or later. 02_sow.md section 7.1; 04_sla.md section 3
Conflicting service credit caps for availability failures: the SOW allows service credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps them at 10%. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2
The service credit amount is not calculable: the SOW says credits are “up to” 25% but gives no formula or scale for determining the actual credit. 02_sow.md section 7.4
The SLA service credit amount is not calculable: it creates an entitlement and a 10% cap but gives no formula or scale for determining the actual credit. 04_sla.md sections 4.1-4.2

Conflicting financial remedy provisions: the SOW provides service credits up to 25% for availability failures, while the SLA makes service credits capped at 10% Customer’s sole financial remedy for failure to meet availability. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md sections 4.2-4.3

Conflicting definitions of “Security Incident”: the DPA defines it broadly to include unauthorised or unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA defines it narrowly as confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of Customer data. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Conflicting Security Incident notification deadlines and triggers: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware, while the SLA allows 72 hours after confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
The SLA references escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2; Annex 3 does not exist. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

The SLA measures response and resolution times from the point Provider acknowledges the Incident, making the response-time target circular or ineffective because response is measured only after acknowledgement. 04_sla.md section 5.4

The DPA says Annex 1 sets out processing details “in full,” but Annex 1 does not fully specify the nature of processing operations and largely repeats only purpose, duration, data subjects and data categories. 03_dpa.md section 3.4 and Annex 1

findings: Circular/inconsistent precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 says the SOW prevails over the MSA. MSA §14.2; SOW §1.2
SOW 1 begins before the MSA exists: the SOW programme commences on 1 March 2027, but the MSA Effective Date is 1 April 2027. MSA Effective Date; SOW §2.2
Programme duration does not fit the MSA initial term: SOW 1 requires a 36-month programme, while the MSA initial term is only 24 months unless renewed. MSA §3.1; SOW §2.1
Conflicting monthly Fee amounts: the MSA states £12,400, while SOW 1 states £12,800. MSA §4.1; SOW §5.1
Conflicting payment periods: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, while SOW 1 allows 45 days. MSA §4.3; SOW §5.3
Conflicting acceptance mechanism: the MSA requires express written acceptance, while SOW 1 provides for deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days of no response. MSA §6.1; SOW §6.3
Broken cross-reference: the MSA says acceptance criteria are in Schedule 1, Section 12, but SOW 1 has no Section 12. MSA §6.2; SOW 1

Deliverables and acceptance criteria are not actually set out in the SOW: SOW 1 refers to a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, but that plan is not included in the contract set and may be changeable outside the agreed contract change process. MSA §§1.3, 2.4, 6.2; SOW §6.1
SOW 1 restricts substitution of named key personnel, but no named key personnel are identified. SOW §3.5
Customer's working hours are used as an operational standard but are not defined. SOW §3.3

Conflicting liability caps: the MSA cap is the Fees paid/payable in the preceding 12 months and says it applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum, while SOW 1 sets a separate £250,000 cap. MSA §§13.1, 13.3; SOW §9.2

Conflicting treatment of data protection liability: the MSA cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum, while the DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law and includes an indemnity for fines. MSA §§13.1, 13.3; DPA §§11.1-11.2
Conflicting professional indemnity insurance limits: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while SOW 1 requires only £2,000,000. MSA §16.1; SOW §9.4
The DPA has a section titled “Precedence” but it contains no operative precedence rule, despite multiple conflicts with the MSA and other schedules. DPA §12

Conflicting governing law: the MSA applies the laws of England and Wales and exclusive English/Welsh courts, while the DPA says it and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. MSA §§15.1-15.2; DPA §§13.1-13.2

Conflicting definition of Confidential Information: the MSA protects only information marked confidential at disclosure, while the DPA says all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. MSA §11.1; DPA §1.4

Internal confidentiality/subcontracting tension: the MSA permits subcontracting without Customer consent but only permits disclosure of Confidential Information to personnel, not subcontractors or other third parties. MSA §§9.3, 11.2

Conflicting subcontractor consent rules for personal-data processing: the MSA permits subcontracting without prior Customer consent, while the DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. MSA §9.3; DPA §5.1

Processing-location conflict: SOW 1 places the delivery team in Bengaluru, India, while the DPA permits processing Customer Personal Data only in the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations. SOW §3.4; DPA §§4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

Conflicting audit rights: the MSA limits Customer to receiving Provider’s annual SOC 2 Type II report and gives no further audit/inspection rights, while the DPA allows annual audits including inspection of premises, systems and records. MSA §§10.2, 12.2; DPA §§9.1-9.2

Internal MSA tension on records access: Provider must make records available on reasonable request, but only “in accordance with” a clause that denies further audit, inspection or attendance rights. MSA §§10.2, 12.2

Conflicting retention/deletion obligations: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry/termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination. MSA §12.4; DPA §§8.2-8.3
Conflicting definitions of Business Day: the MSA uses Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, while the SLA uses Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays. MSA §1.2; SLA §1.1
Conflicting availability commitments: SOW 1 requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the SLA requires 99.9%. SOW §7.2; SLA §3.1

Conflicting start date for service levels: SOW 1 applies platform service levels only from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA states availability obligations without that Phase 3 limitation. SOW §7.1; SLA §3

Conflicting service credit caps and mechanics: SOW 1 allows service credits of up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps monthly credits at 10% and requires automatic application to the next invoice. SOW §7.4; SLA §§4.1-4.2

Conflicting remedial position for availability failures: SOW 1 grants service credits but does not say they are exclusive, while the SLA says service credits are Customer’s sole financial remedy for availability failures. SOW §7.4; SLA §4.3

Conflicting Security Incident definitions: the DPA definition is broad and includes unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; the SLA definition is narrower and requires confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption. DPA §1.6; SLA §7.1

Conflicting Security Incident notification duties: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirmation and to a nominated security contact. DPA §6.1; SLA §7.3
Broken annex reference: the SLA says escalation contacts for Security Incidents are listed in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2. SLA §7.4; DPA annexes

Response-time measurement is circular/toothless: response and resolution targets are measured from Provider’s acknowledgement of the Incident, so the response target is not measured from when the Incident is reported or occurs. SLA §§5.1-5.4
Minor internal inconsistency in data category naming: the DPA body refers to “loyalty scheme identifiers,” while Annex 1 refers to “loyalty identifiers.” DPA §3.3; DPA Annex 1

findings: Conflicting order-of-precedence clauses: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md section 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2
SOW 1 commences before the MSA effective date, even though it is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md section 2.2

The MSA initial term is 24 months, but SOW 1 requires a 36-month programme; the SOW cannot be fully performed within the MSA initial term unless renewal occurs. 01_msa.md section 3.1; 02_sow.md section 2.1

Conflicting termination-for-convenience notice periods: the MSA requires at least 90 days' notice, while SOW 1 requires only 30 days' notice for terminating the SOW. 01_msa.md section 3.3; 02_sow.md section 2.3
Conflicting monthly Fee amounts: the MSA states £12,400, while SOW 1 states £12,800. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1
Conflicting payment periods: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, while SOW 1 allows 45 days. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3

The MSA says no Deliverable is accepted unless Customer expressly confirms acceptance in writing, but SOW 1 provides for deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days without response. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3
The MSA requires Deliverables to be assessed against acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but SOW 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md

Deliverables are not actually fixed in the SOW: the MSA defines Deliverables as items identified in a Statement of Work, but SOW 1 says they are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead. 01_msa.md section 1.3; 02_sow.md section 6.1

The IP assignment trigger is unclear because Provider assigns IP in Deliverables only on payment in full 'for them', but the contract uses monthly service Fees and does not allocate prices to individual Deliverables. 01_msa.md sections 4.1 and 7.2; 02_sow.md section 5

Conflicting audit rights: the MSA limits Customer to receiving Provider's annual SOC 2 Type II report and says there is no further audit/inspection right, while the DPA gives Customer an annual audit right including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

Internal inconsistency in the MSA: Provider must make records available to Customer on reasonable request, but this is made subject to clause 10.2, which says Customer has no further audit, inspection or premises/systems access rights beyond the SOC 2 report. 01_msa.md sections 10.2 and 12.2

Conflicting confidentiality definition: the MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure, while the DPA states all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4

Conflicting subcontracting/subprocessing consent rules: the MSA allows Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA requires Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Conflicting data retention/deletion obligations: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry or termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry or termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2

Conflicting liability regimes: the MSA caps aggregate liability and says the cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum, while the DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

Conflicting liability caps: the MSA cap is based on Fees paid or payable in the preceding 12 months, while SOW 1 sets a fixed £250,000 aggregate cap. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2

Conflicting professional indemnity insurance limits: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while SOW 1 requires at least £2,000,000. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

findings: The order-of-precedence clauses are directly inconsistent: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while the SOW says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md clause 14.2; 02_sow.md clause 1.2
The SOW programme starts before the MSA is effective, even though the SOW is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md clause 2.2

The SOW requires a 36-month programme, but the MSA initial term is only 24 months, leaving the programme extending beyond the initial contractual term unless renewal occurs. 01_msa.md clause 3.1; 02_sow.md clause 2.1

Convenience termination periods conflict for the contract set: the MSA requires at least 90 days' notice, while the SOW allows termination of the SOW on 30 days' notice. 01_msa.md clause 3.3; 02_sow.md clause 2.3
The monthly Fee is stated as £12,400 in the MSA and £12,800 in the SOW. 01_msa.md clause 4.1; 02_sow.md clause 5.1
Payment due dates conflict: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, while the SOW allows 45 days. 01_msa.md clause 4.3; 02_sow.md clause 5.3

The MSA prohibits set-off, deduction or withholding except as required by law or agreed by Provider in writing, but the SLA requires automatic service credits to be applied to the next invoice. 01_msa.md clause 4.5; 04_sla.md clause 4.1

Acceptance provisions conflict: the MSA requires express written acceptance and says no Deliverable is accepted until then, while the SOW provides for deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md clause 6.1; 02_sow.md clause 6.3
The MSA refers to acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md clause 6.2; 02_sow.md generally

Deliverables are not actually listed in the SOW; the SOW points to a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, which conflicts with the MSA definition requiring Deliverables to be identified in a Statement of Work. 01_msa.md clause 1.3; 02_sow.md clause 6.1

The SOW leaves Deliverables to a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, creating uncertainty and potentially allowing changes without the written agreement required by the MSA. 01_msa.md clause 2.4; 02_sow.md clause 6.1

Liability caps conflict: the MSA caps liability at the Fees paid or payable in the preceding 12 months and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum, while the SOW caps liability at £250,000. 01_msa.md clauses 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md clause 9.2

The DPA says no limitation or exclusion of liability applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law, but the MSA imposes a general liability cap and says it applies notwithstanding any Addendum. 01_msa.md clauses 13.1 and 13.3; 03_dpa.md clause 11.1
Professional indemnity insurance limits are inconsistent: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while the SOW states at least £2,000,000. 01_msa.md clause 16.1; 02_sow.md clause 9.4

Audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no audit, inspection or premises/systems access rights beyond receiving the annual SOC 2 Type II report, while the DPA grants annual audit rights including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md clause 10.2; 03_dpa.md clauses 9.1 and 9.2

The MSA is internally inconsistent on records access: clause 12.2 requires Provider to make records available to Customer on reasonable request, but says this is in accordance with clause 10.2, which denies further audit or inspection rights. 01_msa.md clauses 10.2 and 12.2

Record/data retention obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry or termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry or termination. 01_msa.md clause 12.4; 03_dpa.md clause 8.2

Confidential Information is defined inconsistently: the MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure, while the DPA states all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md clause 11.1; 03_dpa.md clause 1.4

Subcontracting/subprocessing consent obligations conflict: the MSA allows Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA prohibits engaging any Subprocessor without Customer's prior written consent to that specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md clause 9.3; 03_dpa.md clause 5.1

Processing location obligations conflict with the delivery location: the SOW says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, but the DPA permits Customer Personal Data processing only in the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations. 02_sow.md clause 3.4; 03_dpa.md clauses 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

The term “Business Day” is defined differently: the MSA uses Monday to Friday excluding public holidays in England and Wales, while the SLA uses Monday to Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md clause 1.2; 04_sla.md clause 1.1
Availability commitments conflict: the SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability. 02_sow.md clause 7.2; 04_sla.md clause 3.1

The start of the availability obligation is inconsistent: the SOW applies service levels from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA contains no Phase 3 limitation and appears to apply generally. 02_sow.md clause 7.1; 04_sla.md section 3

Service credit remedies conflict: the SOW allows service credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps them at 10% of the monthly Fee and makes them the sole financial remedy for availability failure. 02_sow.md clause 7.4; 04_sla.md clauses 4.2 and 4.3

The SOW service credit clause is incomplete because it says credits may be “up to” 25% of the monthly Fee but provides no calculation, tiers or method for determining the actual credit. 02_sow.md clause 7.4

Security Incident is defined inconsistently: the DPA definition covers unauthorised or unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA definition is limited to confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption. 03_dpa.md clause 1.6; 04_sla.md clause 7.1

Security Incident notification deadlines conflict: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness, while the SLA allows 72 hours after confirmation. 03_dpa.md clause 6.1; 04_sla.md clause 7.3
The SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2; Annex 3 does not exist. 04_sla.md clause 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

The DPA governing law conflicts with the MSA: the MSA says the Agreement and disputes are governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA says the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md clause 15.1; 03_dpa.md clause 13.2

The SLA response-time measurement is circular or ineffective: response times are measured from the point Provider acknowledges the Incident, even though acknowledgment is itself the usual response event. 04_sla.md clause 5.4
The SOW restricts substitution of “named key personnel” but does not name any key personnel. 02_sow.md clause 3.5

Service report retention is inconsistent with the MSA's general records retention period: the SLA requires retention only for the duration of the Agreement, while the MSA requires records relating to the Agreement to be retained for 7 years after expiry or termination. 01_msa.md clause 12.4; 04_sla.md clause 6.3

findings: Circular/conflicting precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 says SOW 1 prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md §14.2; 02_sow.md §1.2
The order of precedence does not resolve conflicts between Schedules/Addenda themselves, despite conflicts between SOW 1, the DPA and the SLA. 01_msa.md §14; 02_sow.md; 03_dpa.md; 04_sla.md
SOW 1 starts before the MSA effective date, although it is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date and §3.1; 02_sow.md §2.2

SOW 1 provides for a 36-month programme, while the MSA initial term is only 24 months; the documents do not state what happens if the MSA is not renewed or is terminated before the programme ends. 01_msa.md §3.1-§3.3; 02_sow.md §2.1
Termination notice periods conflict: the MSA allows termination for convenience on 90 days’ notice, while SOW 1 allows termination of the SOW on 30 days’ notice. 01_msa.md §3.3; 02_sow.md §2.3
Monthly Fee is stated as £12,400 in the MSA but £12,800 in SOW 1. 01_msa.md §4.1; 02_sow.md §5.1
Payment period conflicts: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt of invoice, while SOW 1 requires payment within 45 days. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3
Acceptance criteria are referenced as being in Schedule 1, Section 12, but SOW 1 has no Section 12 and no acceptance criteria section. 01_msa.md §6.2; 02_sow.md
Acceptance mechanism conflicts: the MSA requires express written acceptance, while SOW 1 provides for deemed acceptance after five Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md §6.1; 02_sow.md §6.3

Deliverables are supposed to be items identified in a Statement of Work, but SOW 1 says they are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, not in the SOW itself. 01_msa.md §1.3; 02_sow.md §6.1

The phase plan can apparently define Deliverables outside the executed SOW/change-control process, conflicting with the MSA requirement that changes to Services be agreed in writing by both parties. 01_msa.md §2.4; 02_sow.md §6.1

IP assignment occurs on payment in full for Deliverables, but the pricing is a monthly service Fee and does not allocate fees to individual Deliverables, making the assignment trigger unclear. 01_msa.md §7.2; 01_msa.md §4; 02_sow.md §5

The MSA permits subcontracting without Customer consent, while the DPA requires Customer’s prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor; these conflict where subcontracting involves processing Customer Personal Data. 01_msa.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §5.1

The MSA allows subcontracting but confidentiality disclosure is permitted only to personnel who need to know; subcontractors are not expressly included, creating an internal inconsistency. 01_msa.md §9.3; 01_msa.md §11.2

Audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider’s premises or systems beyond receiving the SOC 2 report, while the DPA grants annual audit rights including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md §10.2; 03_dpa.md §9.1-§9.2

Record/data retention conflicts with personal-data deletion: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for seven years after expiry/termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md §12.4; 03_dpa.md §8.2

Service report retention conflicts: the SLA requires service reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement, while the MSA requires all records relating to the Agreement to be retained for seven years after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md §12.4; 04_sla.md §6.3

Liability caps conflict: the MSA caps aggregate liability at Fees paid/payable in the previous 12 months and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum, while SOW 1 sets a separate £250,000 cap. 01_msa.md §13.1 and §13.3; 02_sow.md §9.2

DPA liability provision conflicts with the MSA cap: the DPA says no limitation or exclusion of liability applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law, but the MSA says its liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum. 01_msa.md §13.1-§13.3; 03_dpa.md §11.1
DPA indemnity for fines is inconsistent with the MSA liability cap if the MSA cap applies to all claims under the Agreement. 01_msa.md §13.1-§13.3; 03_dpa.md §11.2
Insurance requirement conflicts: the MSA requires professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000, while SOW 1 requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md §16.1; 02_sow.md §9.4

The same term, “Business Day”, is defined differently: the MSA uses Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, while the SLA uses Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md §1.2; 04_sla.md §1.1

Availability service level conflicts: SOW 1 requires 99.5% monthly availability from Phase 3, while the SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability without the same Phase 3 start limitation. 02_sow.md §7.1-§7.2; 04_sla.md §3.1

Service credit regime conflicts: SOW 1 allows service credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps them at 10% and requires automatic application to the next invoice. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §4.1-§4.2

The SLA says service credits are Customer’s sole financial remedy for availability failure, while SOW 1 does not state that the 25% service credits are sole remedy and the DPA excludes limitations/exclusions for data-protection breaches. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §4.3; 03_dpa.md §11.1

Processing location obligations conflict with the delivery location: SOW 1 says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while the DPA permits processing Customer Personal Data only in the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations. 02_sow.md §3.4; 03_dpa.md §4.1-§4.3 and Annex 2

The DPA states all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked, while the MSA defines Confidential Information only as information marked confidential in writing at disclosure. 01_msa.md §11.1; 03_dpa.md §1.4

Security Incident is defined differently: the DPA definition is broad and includes unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; the SLA definition is narrower and requires confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of Customer data. 03_dpa.md §1.6; 04_sla.md §7.1

Security Incident notification periods conflict: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md §6.1; 04_sla.md §7.3

Governing law conflicts: the MSA is governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA says the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md §15.1; 03_dpa.md §13.1-§13.2

findings: Order of precedence is directly inconsistent: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 says SOW 1 prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md §14.2; 02_sow.md §1.2
SOW 1 starts before the MSA exists: the MSA effective date is 1 April 2027, but the SOW programme commences on 1 March 2027. 01_msa.md Effective Date and §3.1; 02_sow.md §2.2
The MSA initial term is 24 months, but SOW 1 requires a 36-month programme, so the programme extends beyond the initial MSA term unless renewal occurs. 01_msa.md §3.1; 02_sow.md §2.1 and §§4.1-4.4
Convenience termination periods conflict: the MSA requires at least 90 days' notice, while SOW 1 allows termination of the SOW on 30 days' notice. 01_msa.md §3.3; 02_sow.md §2.3
Monthly Fee is inconsistent: the MSA states £12,400, while SOW 1 states £12,800 for the same Services. 01_msa.md §4.1; 02_sow.md §5.1
Payment period is inconsistent: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, while SOW 1 requires payment within 45 days of receipt. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3

Acceptance mechanism conflicts: the MSA says no Deliverable is accepted unless Customer expressly confirms acceptance in writing, while SOW 1 deems acceptance after 5 Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md §6.1; 02_sow.md §6.3
The MSA refers to acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but SOW 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md §6.2; 02_sow.md all sections

SOW 1 does not actually set out acceptance criteria; it says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, leaving the contractual acceptance standard missing or outside the executed documents. 02_sow.md §6.1; 01_msa.md §6.2
Availability service level conflicts: SOW 1 requires 99.5% monthly availability from Phase 3, while the SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability. 02_sow.md §§7.1-7.2; 04_sla.md §3.1
Service credit regime conflicts: SOW 1 allows credits of up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps service credits at 10% of the monthly Fee. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §4.2

Service credit remedy language conflicts: the SLA makes service credits the sole financial remedy for availability failure, while SOW 1 does not state that exclusivity and provides a different credit entitlement. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §4.3
Service credit amount is indeterminate: both SOW 1 and the SLA provide only a maximum credit but no formula or table for calculating the actual credit due. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §§4.1-4.2

Business Day is defined inconsistently: the MSA uses Monday to Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, while the SLA uses Monday to Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md §1.2; 04_sla.md §1.1

The differing Business Day definitions create inconsistent deadlines for maintenance notice, reports, response/resolution targets, and other SLA obligations. 01_msa.md §1.2; 04_sla.md §§2.2, 3.4, 5.2-5.3, 6.1, 8.1

Liability cap conflicts: the MSA caps liability at Fees paid or payable in the preceding 12 months and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum; SOW 1 separately caps Provider liability at £250,000. 01_msa.md §§13.1, 13.3; 02_sow.md §9.2

The DPA attempts to disapply all Agreement limitations and exclusions for DPA/Data Protection Law breaches, but the MSA says its liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum. 01_msa.md §13.3; 03_dpa.md §11.1
Insurance requirement conflicts: the MSA requires professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000, while SOW 1 requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md §16.1; 02_sow.md §9.4

Processing location obligations conflict with the SOW delivery location: the DPA permits processing only in the UK/EEA and lists London and Dublin as approved locations, while SOW 1 requires the delivery team to operate from Bengaluru, India. 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3 and Annex 2; 02_sow.md §3.4

Subcontracting/subprocessor consent obligations conflict: the MSA allows Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §5.1

Audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no audit, inspection, premises or systems access beyond receiving the SOC 2 report, while the DPA allows annual audits including inspection of Provider's premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md §10.2; 03_dpa.md §§9.1-9.2

Record/data retention obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry or termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry or termination. 01_msa.md §12.4; 03_dpa.md §§8.2-8.3

Confidential Information is defined inconsistently: the MSA protects only information marked confidential at disclosure, while the DPA says all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md §11.1; 03_dpa.md §1.4

Security Incident is defined inconsistently: the DPA definition is broad and includes unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA definition is limited to confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of Customer data. 03_dpa.md §1.6; 04_sla.md §7.1

Security Incident notification obligations conflict: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md §6.1; 04_sla.md §7.3
The SLA references escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2; Annex 3 does not exist. 04_sla.md §7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

Governing law conflicts: the MSA says the Agreement and disputes are governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA says the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md §15.1; 03_dpa.md §§13.1-13.2

Jurisdiction/governing law structure is defective: the MSA gives exclusive jurisdiction to the courts of England and Wales for Agreement disputes, while the DPA changes governing law to Ireland without specifying a corresponding jurisdiction and without a precedence clause overriding the MSA. 01_msa.md §15.2; 03_dpa.md §13.2

The DPA says Annex 1 sets out the processing details in full, but Annex 1 omits or only partially states key details such as the nature of processing and does not fully elaborate the subject matter beyond the general Services description. 03_dpa.md §3.4 and Annex 1
SOW 1 restricts substitution of 'named key personnel', but no key personnel are actually named in the SOW, making the restriction uncertain. 02_sow.md §3.5
SOW 1 requires the delivery lead to be available during Customer's working hours, but 'Customer's working hours' is not defined. 02_sow.md §3.3

The SLA measures response and resolution times from the point at which Provider acknowledges the Incident, making the response target circular or self-controlled because the response clock does not start until acknowledgement. 04_sla.md §5.4

MSA internal inconsistency: Provider must make records available to Customer on reasonable request, but the referenced clause says Customer has no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems, leaving unclear what record access is actually permitted. 01_msa.md §§10.2, 12.2

SLA report retention conflicts or is at least inconsistent with the MSA record-retention period: the SLA requires retaining service reports only for the duration of the Agreement, while the MSA requires records relating to the Agreement to be retained for 7 years after expiry or termination. 04_sla.md §6.3; 01_msa.md §12.4
unmatched: SOW 1 does not actually set out acceptance criteria; it says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, leaving the contractual acceptance standard missing or outside the executed documents. 02_sow.md §6.1; 01_msa.md §6.2

Service credit remedy language conflicts: the SLA makes service credits the sole financial remedy for availability failure, while SOW 1 does not state that exclusivity and provides a different credit entitlement. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §4.3
Service credit amount is indeterminate: both SOW 1 and the SLA provide only a maximum credit but no formula or table for calculating the actual credit due. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §§4.1-4.2

The differing Business Day definitions create inconsistent deadlines for maintenance notice, reports, response/resolution targets, and other SLA obligations. 01_msa.md §1.2; 04_sla.md §§2.2, 3.4, 5.2-5.3, 6.1, 8.1

The DPA says Annex 1 sets out the processing details in full, but Annex 1 omits or only partially states key details such as the nature of processing and does not fully elaborate the subject matter beyond the general Services description. 03_dpa.md §3.4 and Annex 1
SOW 1 restricts substitution of 'named key personnel', but no key personnel are actually named in the SOW, making the restriction uncertain. 02_sow.md §3.5
SOW 1 requires the delivery lead to be available during Customer's working hours, but 'Customer's working hours' is not defined. 02_sow.md §3.3

The SLA measures response and resolution times from the point at which Provider acknowledges the Incident, making the response target circular or self-controlled because the response clock does not start until acknowledgement. 04_sla.md §5.4
