Audit rights conflict: the MSA limits Customer to receiving the SOC 2 report and states Customer has no further audit/inspection rights, while the DPA permits audits including inspection of premises, systems and records. MSA clause 10.2; DPA sections 9.1-9.2

Internal MSA ambiguity: Provider must make records available on reasonable request, but only in accordance with clause 10.2, which says Customer has no further audit, inspection or premises/systems access rights. MSA clauses 10.2 and 12.2

Retention/deletion conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry or termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry or termination. MSA clause 12.4; DPA section 8.2

Confidential Information is defined inconsistently: the MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure, while the DPA says all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. MSA clause 11.1; DPA section 1.4

Liability cap conflict: the MSA caps aggregate liability at the previous 12 months' Fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum; the SOW instead caps liability at £250,000. MSA clauses 13.1 and 13.3; SOW section 9.2

Data protection liability conflict: the DPA says no Agreement limitation or exclusion applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law, directly conflicting with the MSA liability cap and its statement that the cap applies notwithstanding Addenda. MSA clauses 13.1 and 13.3; DPA section 11.1
Insurance requirement conflict: the MSA requires professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires only £2,000,000. MSA clause 16.1; SOW section 9.4

Governing law conflict: the MSA applies the laws of England and Wales to the Agreement and disputes, while the DPA applies the laws of the Republic of Ireland to the DPA and disputes arising out of it. MSA clause 15.1; DPA sections 13.1-13.2
The DPA section titled “Precedence” contains no actual precedence rule, leaving DPA conflicts with the MSA unresolved except by the MSA’s MSA-prevails clause. DPA section 12

Business Day is defined inconsistently: the MSA uses Monday-Friday excluding public holidays in England and Wales; the SLA uses Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays. MSA clause 1.2; SLA section 1.1
Availability obligation conflict: the SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability from Phase 3, while the SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability. SOW sections 7.1-7.2; SLA section 3.1

Timing of availability obligations conflicts: the SOW applies platform service levels only from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA imposes availability obligations without any Phase 3 limitation. SOW section 7.1; SLA section 3
Service credit amount conflicts: the SOW allows service credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps them at 10%. SOW section 7.4; SLA section 4.2

Remedies conflict: the SLA says service credits are Customer’s sole financial remedy for availability failure, while the SOW and MSA do not limit Customer to that sole remedy and the SOW provides a different credit regime. SLA section 4.3; SOW section 7.4; MSA clauses 13.1-13.3

Security Incident is defined inconsistently: the DPA covers any unauthorised or unlawful access to, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption. DPA section 1.6; SLA section 7.1

Security Incident notification timing conflicts: the DPA requires notice within 24 hours of becoming aware, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming the incident. DPA section 6.1; SLA section 7.3
The SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2. SLA section 7.4; DPA annexes

SLA response-time measurement is defective: response and resolution times are measured from Provider’s acknowledgement, so the response target is measured from the response itself and Provider can delay the start of the clock by not acknowledging. SLA section 5.4
Support hours are ambiguous because 08:00 to 18:00 is stated without a time zone, despite the documents involving the UK, India, Ireland and a US-holiday Business Day definition. SLA section 2.2

The DPA says Annex 1 sets out processing details in full, but Annex 1 omits or only partially states key processing details such as the nature of processing and specific processing operations. DPA section 3.4 and Annex 1
unmatched: The SOW programme commences before the MSA effective date, even though the SOW is issued under the MSA. MSA Effective Date; SOW section 2.2

Deliverables are not actually identified in the SOW; they are said to be listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, conflicting with the MSA definition of Deliverable as an item identified in a Statement of Work. MSA clause 1.3; SOW section 6.1
The SOW restricts substitution of named key personnel, but no named key personnel are identified. SOW section 3.5

Timing of availability obligations conflicts: the SOW applies platform service levels only from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA imposes availability obligations without any Phase 3 limitation. SOW section 7.1; SLA section 3

SLA response-time measurement is defective: response and resolution times are measured from Provider’s acknowledgement, so the response target is measured from the response itself and Provider can delay the start of the clock by not acknowledging. SLA section 5.4
Support hours are ambiguous because 08:00 to 18:00 is stated without a time zone, despite the documents involving the UK, India, Ireland and a US-holiday Business Day definition. SLA section 2.2

findings: Circular/contradictory precedence: the MSA says it prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md section 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2
The SOW programme starts on 1 March 2027, one month before the MSA effective date of 1 April 2027, even though the SOW is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md section 2.2

Conflicting convenience termination notice periods: the MSA requires at least 90 days' notice, while the SOW may be terminated on 30 days' notice; because of the precedence conflict it is unclear which governs the services. 01_msa.md section 3.3; 02_sow.md section 2.3
Conflicting monthly Fee amounts: the MSA states £12,400, while SOW 1 states £12,800 for the same Services. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1
Conflicting payment periods: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt of an undisputed invoice, while SOW 1 allows 45 days. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3

Conflicting acceptance mechanism: the MSA requires express written acceptance and says no Deliverable is accepted until then, while SOW 1 provides deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days of no response. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3
The MSA requires Deliverables to be assessed against acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but SOW 1 has no Section 12 and no acceptance criteria there. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md

Deliverables are not actually identified in the SOW; they are said to be listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, which conflicts with the MSA definition requiring Deliverables to be identified in a Statement of Work and creates an external/uncontrolled deliverables list. 01_msa.md section 1.3; 02_sow.md section 6.1
The SOW refers to “named key personnel” but no key personnel are named, making the substitution restriction inoperable or unclear. 02_sow.md section 3.5
Conflicting liability caps: the MSA caps liability at Fees paid/payable in the preceding 12 months, while SOW 1 caps Provider's liability at £250,000. 01_msa.md section 13.1; 02_sow.md section 9.2

The MSA says its liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum, while the DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 01_msa.md section 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

The SOW excludes indirect or consequential loss, but the DPA says no limitation or exclusion of liability in the Agreement applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 02_sow.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
Conflicting professional indemnity insurance requirements: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while SOW 1 requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Conflicting audit rights: the MSA limits Customer to receiving an annual SOC 2 Type II report and gives no further audit/inspection rights, while the DPA permits annual audits including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

Conflicting subcontracting/subprocessor consent rights: the MSA allows Provider to subcontract without Customer consent, while the DPA requires Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Conflicting confidentiality definition: the MSA treats only information marked confidential in writing as Confidential Information, while the DPA says all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4

Conflicting data retention/deletion obligations: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry/termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2

The SOW states that the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, but the DPA allows Customer Personal Data to be processed only in the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved processing locations. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

Conflicting governing law: the MSA and disputes under it are governed by England and Wales law, while the DPA and disputes under it are governed by the laws of the Republic of Ireland, despite the DPA forming part of the Agreement. 01_msa.md section 15.1; 03_dpa.md sections 12.1 and 13.1-13.2

The DPA says Annex 1 sets out the processing details in full, but Annex 1 does not fully state the nature of processing and only provides high-level purpose, duration, data subjects and data categories. 03_dpa.md section 3.4 and Annex 1

Conflicting definitions of Business Day: the MSA defines it as Monday to Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, while the SLA defines it as Monday to Saturday excluding US federal holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1
Conflicting availability service levels: SOW 1 requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md section 7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

Conflicting start of service-level obligations: SOW 1 says platform service levels apply from the start of Phase 3, while the SLA contains no Phase 3 limitation and appears to apply generally. 02_sow.md section 7.1; 04_sla.md sections 3-5

Conflicting service credit caps/remedies: SOW 1 provides service credits of up to 25% of the monthly Fee, while the SLA caps monthly service credits at 10% and makes them the sole financial remedy for availability failure. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md sections 4.2-4.3

The SLA requires Provider to apply service credits automatically, while SOW 1 merely says Customer is entitled to credits of up to 25% and gives no automatic application mechanism; the credit mechanism is inconsistent. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.1

Conflicting definitions of Security Incident: the DPA definition covers any unauthorised or unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data, while the SLA definition is limited to confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of Customer data. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

Conflicting Security Incident notification deadlines and triggers: the DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware, while the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming the incident. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3
The SLA references escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has only Annex 1 and Annex 2; Annex 3 does not exist. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

The SLA measures both Response and Resolution times from the point Provider acknowledges the Incident, making the Response target circular/nonsensical because response time should measure time to acknowledgement or first response, not from acknowledgement. 04_sla.md section 5.4

Conflicting report/record retention periods: the SLA requires service reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement, while the MSA requires Provider to retain records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry or termination. 04_sla.md section 6.3; 01_msa.md section 12.4

The SOW refers to “named key personnel” but no key personnel are named, making the substitution restriction inoperable or unclear. 02_sow.md section 3.5

The SOW excludes indirect or consequential loss, but the DPA says no limitation or exclusion of liability in the Agreement applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 02_sow.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

The DPA says Annex 1 sets out the processing details in full, but Annex 1 does not fully state the nature of processing and only provides high-level purpose, duration, data subjects and data categories. 03_dpa.md section 3.4 and Annex 1
